💡 Key Takeaways
  • von Next Generation am 05.03.2025 in den Kategorien Team Portraits mit 0 Kommentaren.
  • Industry observers note that inter Milan’s U19 team is the only side in this season’s UEFA Youth League to have won all their matches so far, finishing the group stage of the “Youth Champions League” in first place.
  • Inter Milan generally builds up in a nominal 4-3-3 shape.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

von Next Generation am 05.03.2025 in den Kategorien Team Portraits mit 0 Kommentaren.

Industry observers note that inter Milan’s U19 team is the only side in this season’s UEFA Youth League to have won all their matches so far, finishing the group stage of the “Youth Champions League” in first place. They also secured victory in the knockout playoff round and will now face Bayern Munich U19 in the Round of 16. This analysis will take a closer look at Inter Milan’s tactical structures and mechanisms under head coach Andrea Zanchetta in the Youth League while also considering possible approaches against them.

Inter Milan generally builds up in a nominal 4-3-3 shape. A key role is played by the midfield trio, consisting of the two number eights, Topalovic and Venturini, alongside the single pivot, Mattia Zanchetta. Zanchetta frequently drops between the center-backs, taking on a key role in deep buildup, while the two eights serve as connectors and overload players in the transition from deeper buildup into more advanced areas. According to the Italian Wikipedia, head coach Andrea Zanchetta is the father of Mattia Zanchetta.

Recent findings suggest that inter’s defensive structure varies depending on the opponent and pressing height. In mid-block and high-pressing phases, they defend in a narrow 4-3-2-1, a compact 4-3-3, or a 4-4-2, depending on the opposition’s structure. When defending deeper, they shift into a 4-1-4-1, with Zanchetta holding his position as the single pivot shielding the backline.

As the central striker, either Lavelli or Spinaccè leads the line. Since both share a similar physical, robust playing style, this analysis will primarily refer to Spinaccè, who has started in recent matches. On the right wing, Pieri is a fixed starter, known for his strong 1v1 abilities. On the opposite flank, head coach Zanchetta has rotated more frequently, but he has consistently relied on technically strong, dribble-oriented wingers.

Sources indicate that to build up against high pressing, Inter relies on certain patterns that make it more difficult for the opponent to press successfully. A frequent observation is that the center-backs move wide while the full-backs push up along the touchline. At the same time, the single pivot Zanchetta and/or the number eight Topalovic drop deep to lure the opposition’s midfield out of the center. The longer the possession phase lasts near their own penalty area, the more likely it is that both the pivot and the number eight drop into the center-back positions. The now-vacated central space is occupied by the other number eight, Venturini, and the frequently dropping center-forward Spinaccè. When buildup occurs on the right side, Topalovic often stays on the far side to stretch the central area further. The wingers act as additional passing options by tucking into the half-spaces. From this structure, the opponent can be bypassed using vertical-layoff combinations in the half-space.

According to recent reports, the primary goal of the buildup is often a pass to the target man Spinaccè, who either uses Venturini as a layoff option or directly switches play to the wing. By pulling apart the central space through the movements of Topalovic and Zanchetta, the goalkeeper typically initiates buildup through the wide center-backs, who frequently play a direct pass to the dropping striker via the now-open diagonal deep passing lane. Particularly noteworthy are the anticipatory movements of the layoff options in these combinations. The attacking number eight, Venturini, excels at positioning himself to receive layoffs from the back-to-goal striker Spinaccè, ensuring continuity in progression.

Sources indicate that if only Zanchetta drops between the center-backs to form the resulting back three, the left-sided number eight, Topalovic, and the right-sided number eight, Venturini, move into the half-spaces to receive when the center-backs are in possession. Through a vertical-layoff combination involving one of the eights, the now-advancing pivot Zanchetta, and the dropping center-forward Spinaccè, the midfield can be quickly bypassed, allowing the ball to be switched to the wing in the opponent’s half.

According to recent reports, to effectively press Inter’s buildup directly, a hybrid pressing approach combining man- and space-orientation could be a viable strategy. A particularly crucial role could be assigned to the ball-far holding midfielder, who could operate positionally to close passing lanes, preventing deep balls into the target man Spinaccè while also ensuring that the central space cannot be stretched. Additionally, an aggressive step-out from a center-back would be necessary to avoid numerical inferiority in midfield. On the ball-near side, increased pressure could be applied through man-oriented marking to maximize pressing intensity.

Industry observers note that through hybrid pressing, the center can be occupied, and the typical passing lane can be blocked. The downside is the numerical disadvantage on the ball-far side and the man-to-man marking on the last line.

It has been revealed that even against teams that press deeper, certain patterns can be observed in Inter Milan U19’s buildup. From their usual 4-3-3 structure with a single pivot and two number eights, they transition into a three-man buildup shape against opponents using a two-striker system. To achieve this, Zanchetta drops between the center-backs, who move wider, while the full-backs push higher along the touchline. However, Zanchetta plays a flexible role, shifting between a central center-back position and his original pivot role, making himself available in midfield depending on the situation.

Recent findings suggest that this three-man buildup creates new passing connections designed to pose problems for the opponent. A key role is played by Topalovic and Venturini, who drop closer to the buildup to fill the emerging gap between the midfield and the first buildup line. The buildup is primarily conducted through the half-spaces and the wide areas. The ball-near number eight moves into the half-space to overload it, while Venturini, from the right half-space, moves into an advanced position, and Topalovic, from the left half-space, stays closer to the buildup zone, occasionally even dropping into the first line. The ball-far number eight occupies the center.

It has been revealed that due to this asymmetry between the two eights, the wingers on each side have slightly different roles. On the right side, where Venturini often occupies the advanced half-space, the right winger stays wider, creating double width with the full-back. On the left side, since Topalovic supports deeper in the buildup, the left winger frequently moves into the half-space, opening the lane for the overlapping full-back on the outside.

Sources indicate that additionally, Spinaccè overloads the half-space by shifting ball-near and dropping deeper. Particularly on the left side, a diagonal deep pass from the wide-positioned center-back in the back three can find either the winger or the striker in a diagonal alignment. This escadinha staggering provides multiple layoff options. The ultimate goal after playing through the half-space is to create a 1v1 situation on the wing, allowing the dribbling-strong wingers or advancing full-backs to be isolated and attack down the flank.

Through the typical half-space overload, the wide area can be opened for a 1v1 situation involving the advancing full-back.

The follow-up action is usually a cross into the penalty area. This is typically occupied by the aerially strong striker, the ball-far winger, and Topalovic. In the second line, Zanchetta and Venturini can win second balls.

One of the key aspects of Inter Milan’s game is their man-marking high press. With the exception of the match against Manchester City, coach Zanchetta’s team has consistently relied on man-marking and aggressive pressing in advanced areas. This approach frequently creates dangerous transition moments by forcing early turnovers.

While striker Spinaccè and the right winger are primarily responsible for initiating the press, Topalovic and Zanchetta operate in central areas. Zanchetta, known for his strength in duels, pushes far forward from his usual deeper pivot position to press opposing midfielders and win the ball in central areas. The offensively oriented number eight, Venturini, is deliberately kept out of direct 1v1 defensive duels in the center and instead takes responsibility for a potentially advancing full-back. On the opposite side, the opposing full-back is covered by Inter’s winger.

Industry observers note that the pressing is almost always triggered by Spinaccè from a slightly left-sided position. He presses the goalkeeper while blocking the passing lane to the left center-back. This forces the opponent’s buildup toward the wing, where Inter engages in their man-oriented pressing. In particular, the ball-far midfielder, Topalovic, often abandons his direct man-marking after the opponent is forced to play toward the far-side wing. Instead, he drops back toward the defensive line to create numerical superiority and ensure that the center-backs can step out aggressively without leaving gaps in the last line.

According to recent reports, A possible solution against this man-marking press could involve putting the opposing center-backs in a dilemma. By having the strikers drop deep, they could force the center-backs to abandon their cover in the last line. Since Inter Milan’s full-backs are less dominant in defensive 1v1 situations, wingers making deep diagonal runs into the vacated spaces could create a favorable scenario. Once the press is triggered, these wingers should be played into 1v1 situations through deep passes. This either forces the physically strong center-backs out of the last line or creates a numerical superiority in midfield that can be exploited.

Industry observers note that another possible approach could involve a high-positioned, inverted left-back. By dropping into the space between the opponent’s forward and midfield lines, he could create a central 1v1 against Venturini, who is not as defensively strong.

In a recent development, depending on the opponent, Inter may drop slightly deeper and defend in a 4-3-3 or 4-4-2 mid-block shape. This adjustment depends on the opposition’s buildup structure. The fundamental goal is to maintain numerical parity against the opponent’s buildup line, allowing Inter to transition into aggressive man-marking and press forward. Against a three-man buildup, they press in a 4-3-3 shape, while against a four-man buildup, they shift into a 4-4-2. A key emphasis is placed on central compactness, making it more difficult for the opponent to progress through the middle.

According to recent reports, once the ball is shifted to one side, Inter looks to apply pressure and enforce man-marking, similar to their approach in the high press. Zanchetta frequently pushes forward aggressively on the ball-near side to put pressure on the opponent’s central midfielders and create ball-winning opportunities.

According to recent reports, while the full-backs also push high to apply pressure, the center-backs primarily serve as defensive cover. However, when the opposition’s strikers drop deeper, the center-backs do not follow them to avoid leaving gaps in the defensive line. Instead, Inter presses with one less player in the first line to compensate for the opponent’s numerical superiority in midfield. Even in these situations, the opponent is guided toward one side, where Inter then looks to regain possession. To execute this, the first pressing line must initially cut off the passing lane to one of the defenders, allowing the opponent to maintain more possession and reducing Inter’s ability to transition into their man-marking press.

Especially in the low block, Inter Milan manages to make the field so compact that progression becomes extremely difficult. From a 4-1-4-1 structure, they compress the space just in front of their own penalty area. Zanchetta operates between the lines as a space-oriented pivot in front of the defense. When the opponent shifts play to one side, Zanchetta also moves laterally and looks to engage an opposing player.

As the central players shift heavily toward the ball side, defensive numerical superiority is often created near the ball, allowing Inter to apply pressure. The ball-far number eight secures the central area, while the ball-far winger stays wide when the opponent maintains width on both flanks to prevent switches of play. This enables the last defensive line to shift further toward the ball side, allowing the ball-near center-back to step out aggressively while still being covered.

According to recent reports, inter Milan’s U19 team manages to challenge opponents through a well-organized and versatile defensive structure. They can adapt to various pressing heights, with their difficult-to-play man-marking high press frequently creating dangerous transition moments close to the opponent’s goal.

In possession, Inter also succeeds in reaching the opponent’s penalty area frequently through a very direct approach aimed at attacking depth. The key to this is a well-coordinated midfield and a striker who can act as a target player, holding up the ball with his back to goal. Most of Inter’s combinations are designed to create a 1v1 situation on the wing, where both the advancing full-backs and the wingers are very difficult to defend.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, these remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see.
  • It has been revealed that not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net.
  • Sources indicate that this meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, these remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club that has spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League. After making eight new signings, they have so far scored zero goals and won zero points.

It has been revealed that not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net. The summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is therefore already drifting away, to the sound of an alarmingly familiar soundtrack: boos from the home supporters at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Sources indicate that this meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it. Yet it was Newcastle, still adjusting to the loss of three key players this summer, who looked the more unified group and more organised team.

It proved to be a truly glorious evening for the visiting supporters, who not only delighted in their team’s victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs a few weeks ago, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee. That price tag is not his fault but it is his burden, and in time he will need to shoulder it more impressively than he did here.

Roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, can rightly say that it will take time for his new group to develop the cohesion he needs. The worrying reality for Spurs, though, is that his opposite number had far less time to work with his players and far less money to reshape his squad. Matthias Jaissle appears to be a man with a defined initiative, and an ability to convey it. Newcastle improved considerably after half-time, which spoke volumes of Jaissle’s work. “He is the best signing of Newcastle so far,” remarked Yoane Wissa of his new coach.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc.

For Spurs, so much of it would have felt painfully similar to last season, when they won only three home games in the Premier League. They played some pretty football in bursts, but not at the crucial points of the game. The second half, especially, was pockmarked with moments of despair. There was Mathys Tel’s free-kick that almost flew into Islington, for example, and Mateus Fernandes falling over when running onto a pass in the penalty area.

De Zerbi stated he was sorry for the fans and for the club, and suggested his team is not properly prepared for this campaign. “Maybe we are not ready yet,” he said. “For many, many reasons we are not ready yet.”.

"I have no panic, I know very well where I'm going" Roberto De Zerbi apologises to Spurs fans after the defeat to Newcastle 🔊 pic.twitter.com/83DntjG5ZH.

Newcastle’s two goals, much like Brentford’s three last weekend, exposed the enduring frailties in the Spurs defence. Anthony Elanga’s opener stemmed from a long pass over the top of the home side’s high line, while Wissa’s acrobatic effort came from a corner kick that Spurs could not handle. Neither strike, it would be safe to say, was the result of world-class attacking play.

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm.

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY.

Industry observers note that “After the first goal we lost confidence,” stated De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”.

According to recent reports, to be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

"He's got an opportunity to be the main man"Jamie Redknapp praises Nico Gonzalez's performance on his debut 👏 pic.twitter.com/1ga3tsxXHA.

Sources indicate that might it have been different for Spurs if £75m winger Savio had been available? The Brazilian was electrifying on his debut in midweek, when he scored against Charlton Athletic in the League Cup, yet was unavailable here due to a minor injury. It instead fell to another signing from City, Omar Marmoush, to lead the attack. He was busy and floaty but never truly hurt Newcastle.

In a recent development, there are more changes to come at Spurs before Tuesday’s deadline. De Zerbi revealed after the game that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave the club.

Industry observers note that at least the issues facing his players appear clear to De Zerbi. His list of areas to improve was lengthy – he spoke of strengthening the connection between the players, the quality of their play, their work in the defensive phase and the distances between them – but he also insisted he loves them and remains confident in the club’s project. At this rate, though, the fans might not share that confidence for much longer.

Recent findings suggest that the Tottenham boss told BBC Sport: “Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded I think we played better than Newcastle. We lost ball possession in the first half because we didn’t defend in the right way, the distance between the defenders and attackers was too major. We can improve in the defensive phases but today was an unfair result.

“At the beginning of the second half we had some chance to create the potential chances. We created many chances to score, we have to improve the last decision, because that will make a difference. At the end we are disappointed for the result and our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team I think we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham.

“We are working to be good on the pitch, if you believe in work and training then you have to improve day by day.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Newcastle’s head coach said: “It was incredible and I’m really proud. We are really proud as a club, as a coaching staff to see a team on the pitch delivering the match initiative at a high level already, but also seeing players fully committed to what we’re doing. This is a good start and a moment to enjoy.

“We also did well last week against Liverpool, therefore it was a step in the right direction again against a strong opponent with huge signings during the transfer window. This is something we were aware of, but how we handled that challenge was amazing.”.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc.

According to recent reports, "With the fans behind us, no one can stop us" 🖤Yoane Wissa reacts to Newcastle's win at Spurs! pic.twitter.com/itaiVO3Kx1.

After a tumultuous summer, Jaissle has ushered in a new era of hope and positivity at Newcastle, with Wissa and Elanga reborn in attack.

"Oh Jaissle, I can boogie..." 🎶🕺 pic.twitter.com/FmvC2DrLMO.

In a recent development, 2 - Anthony Elanga is the first player to score in both of Newcastle United's first two Premier League games of a campaign since Alan Shearer in 2003-04.Footsteps. pic.twitter.com/VZ3hXEbpG7.

2 - Tottenham Hotspur have lost their opening two matches of a league campaign without scoring for the first time since the 1974-75 season.Concerning. pic.twitter.com/N8izpVYslx.

Industry observers note that jaissle records his first ever Premier League win, heaping more misery upon Tottenham, who begin the season with two defeats. Excellent second-half finishes from Elanga and Wissa have given the visitors a superb three points in the capital.

Recent findings suggest that YOU MAGSSSS! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/PRM8yYg7Yl.

It has been revealed that barnes attempts to latch onto a ball in behind, but Kinsky races out to claim. Spurs then almost half-heartedly come forward as Udogie tries to find Marmoush with a powerful cross. The new Spurs forward gets some contact on the ball, but it ricochets to Hall, who hacks it clear. Newcastle then make a late change as Toure replaces Barnes.

Industry observers note that fernandes clips a pinpoint cross into Marmoush. The Egyptian shoots via a first-time volley, but his tame attempt is easily gathered by Hornicek.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

According to recent reports, nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

Newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his new surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

It has been revealed that despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in fresh boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

Newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We're now a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while we're still weeks away from the unofficial start of trade season (Dec.
  • Firm rumors are still in short supply, but we're at least getting some early buzz on who prepares to do what in the months to come.
  • The 14-3 Los Angeles Lakers are headed for a titanic clash with the San Antonio Spurs on Friday that will presumably put one of those two teams in pole position in the Western Conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We're now a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while we're still weeks away from the unofficial start of trade season (Dec. 15), we've seen enough basketball for teams to at least begin making plans for the upcoming transaction cycle. Teams are starting to know how good they are, what sort of holes they're dealing with and what the market is going to look like as we draw closer to the February trade deadline.

Firm rumors are still in short supply, but we're at least getting some early buzz on who prepares to do what in the months to come. So let's check in on what has made the rounds lately.

The 14-3 Los Angeles Lakers are headed for a titanic clash with the San Antonio Spurs on Friday that will presumably put one of those two teams in pole position in the Western Conference. Last Friday, however, head of basketball operations Rob Pelinka did a pregame interview with Spectrum SportsNet in which he made it clear he plans to be aggressive ahead of February's deadline.

Recent findings suggest that "We'll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see," Pelinka remarked. "We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can. Don't want to get too far over our skis with a hot start, because you don't want to get big-headed, but clearly the way it's gone so far, it's been great and we hope it continues.".

Recent findings suggest that the Lakers are very limited in terms of tradable draft capital because of their big July swing for Walker Kessler. They only have one first-round asset available, and it's only swap rights in 2032. They picked up two useful second-round picks in the Deandre Ayton trade, though, giving them three in total. That's not enough for a blockbuster, but it's helpful liquidity. Further, the Lakers are relatively financially flexible going into the deadline as well. They're barely over the luxury-tax line and have around $8 million in room beneath their first apron hard cap, allowing them to potentially make a somewhat unbalanced trade if the need presents itself.

So, what would the Lakers be looking for at the deadline? Two obvious needs stand out:.

According to recent reports, as Marc Stein noted, the Los Angeles Clippers have moved to a veteran-only starting lineup, with Darius Garland, Rui Hachimura, Derrick Jones Jr., Max Strus and Brook Lopez opening games lately. Brandon Ingram, returning Monday, is sure to join that group, and Kris Dunn is a central part of their rotation. All of these players but Ingram and Garland are on expiring deals, and Stein noted that the Clippers are "regarded as a certain seller" ahead of the trade deadline.

And, well, that makes plenty of sense. The Clippers were just stripped of five first-round picks in the Kawhi Leonard scandal. Those expiring contracts belong to players who almost certainly won't be a part of the next great Clipper team, but they could help replenish the team's draft capital moving forward.

In a recent development, the Clippers are, by far, the most versatile seller on the market right now. In theory, they could burnish just about any contender. Need defense? Jones and Dunn have you covered. Offense? Strus and Hachimura are proven playoff snipers. The center market is in the middle of a supply-demand crisis. Lopez has been sensational this season and could give any contender a solid 20 minutes per night. With Keaton Wagler in the building, it's hard to imagine they'd even shut the door on a good enough Garland offer. Expect the Clippers to live in the rumor mill for the next few months. They have several players who could legitimately impact the championship hunt.

It has been revealed that last week, SNY dropped a stunner of a rumor: that the Utah Jazz, loaded with young guards and off to a terrible start, had had internal conversations about pursuing Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving. The rumor didn't make much sense in the moment, and The Salt Lake Tribune reported Monday that the Jazz "don't appear to have any real interest" in the future Hall of Famer.

They have, however, talked trade with the team we just discussed: the Clippers. Those conversations began with "various Clippers bigs" and have moved on to wing depth, of which the Clippers have plenty. The Jazz are reportedly casting a wide net in pursuit of help.

The 3-15 Jazz have been among the NBA's biggest disappointments this season. A lot of that has been the result of injuries, with Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen out now and Jusuf Nurkić having not yet debuted this season. The Jazz are painfully thin in the front court at this point, and the early partnership between Keyonte George and Darryn Peterson in the backcourt has yielded mixed results.

Casting a wide net makes sense since the Jazz could theoretically use help basically anywhere. More of a playmaking guard to balance out the score-first instincts that George and Peterson bring would make sense. Wing depth, especially defense-first wing depth, would help address a major weakness. Dunn is a former Jazz player. And of course, adding some size to deal with all of those injuries would probably have the biggest immediate impact. Utah doesn't control its own first-round pick this year. The Jazz benefit from losing in no way, and that has seemingly made them eager to try to fight an uphill battle back into the Western Conference Play-In race.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway.
  • Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing.
  • It has been revealed that free agent catcher Tyler Stephenson has agreed to a three-year contract to return to the Reds, reports ESPN.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples. Just recently, for instance, the Newly introduced York Mets landed the biggest fish in the pond by signing ace Tarik Skubal to a record contract. Not long after, the Chicago Cubs fortified their rotation with Trevor Rogers and their outfield with Teruaki Sato, and Freddy Peralta is headed to the Baltimore Orioles. More's surely to come before lockout day arrives.

Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Tuesday's supply just below.

It has been revealed that free agent catcher Tyler Stephenson has agreed to a three-year contract to return to the Reds, reports ESPN. The deal is worth $30 million and includes an opt-out after the second year. Cincinnati selected Stephenson, 30, with the No. 11 pick in the 2015 draft, and he's played his entire career with the Reds. We ranked him as the 46th-best free agent available.

It has been revealed that the Reds will again pair Stephenson with glove-first backup Jose Trevino behind the plate. Cincinnati now figures to turn their attention to the pitching staff, both the rotation and bullpen. Hunter Greene's UCL surgery means Andrew Abbott and Chase Burns are the only locks for the rotation, though Nick Lodolo will have a spot as long as he's healthy.

The Yankees are among the many teams with interest in top free agent reliever Adrian Morejon, reports the New York Post. Some teams view him as a potential starter, though there were reports earlier this month that he prefers to stay in the bullpen. The Phillies, meanwhile, are not considered a serious candidate to sign Morejon, according to The Athletic. We ranked him as the second-best free agent available this offseason, in part due to his potential to start.

Adding to the bullpen has been the Yankees' primary focus so far this offseason. Closer David Bednar accepted the qualifying offer, they re-signed lefty matchup guy Tim Hill, and signed Jonathan Loáisiga and Tim Hill as free agents. At some point they will need to add to their lineup, particularly at third base, but there's always room for a reliever like Morejon in the bullpen.

The Philadelphia Phillies are open to moving Trea Turner off of shortstop given that he's now a pronounced defensive liability. Speaking of openness, veteran shortstop Corey Seager of the Texas Rangers is willing to waive his no-trade clause to join the Phillies and upgrade the position for them, NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.

Industry observers note that now 32, Seager will always have health and durability concerns, but he remains a plus defensive shortstop who produces well at the plate by positional standards. Signed to a 10-year, $325 million deal prior to the 2022 season (just before the last lockout, in fact), Seager is owed another $155 million through the 2031 season. The Rangers are reportedly looking to shake things up. The Phillies, meantime, are trying to keep their contention window open. It's a fit both ways, at least in theory. Such a move would likely mean a move to the outfield for Turner, who himself has very little trade value thanks to his ongoing decline and major contract.

It has been revealed that even in a down 2026 year, Jazz Chisholm Jr. put up 19 homers and stole 41 bases while manning an up-the-middle position. Still just 28 years of age, he figures to have a healthy market this offseason. Speaking of which, the Washington Nationals are one of multiple teams presently in contact with Chisholm, FanSided reports.

Sources indicate that earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Chisholm as the No. 6 free agent in the current class. Here's part of that write-up:.

Sources indicate that "In what was his worst season as a hitter since his rookie year in 2021, Chisholm was still a league-average bat in 2026, and his top-shelf defense and baserunning still landed him at 3.5 WAR. Chisholm is a style-over-substance player who is not for everyone, but his second base defense and near-MLB-best baserunning skills give him a very high floor. He's a reasonable bet for 20-ish home runs with the potential to go 30-30, and Chisholm has improved his plate discipline enough to run walk rates north of 10% the last two years. The downside is his propensity to swing and miss. Chisholm has posted below-average in-zone contact rates throughout his career and contact rates that low always come with risk. That risk is mitigated somewhat by the secondary skills (defense, etc.) and the fact that Chisholm will play the entire 2027 season at age 29. You probably don't want him as your best or second-best player, but he's also an overqualified No. 6-7 hitter who brings so much else to the table.".

The Cleveland Guardians have agreed to a free-agent contract with left-hander Kris Bubic, Sportsnet reports. The contract is for $17.5 million over one year, according to ESPN. Bubic, 29, made nine starts for the Kansas City Royals last season, and after the trade to the Los Angeles Dodgers, he was used out of the bullpen. Bubic has an outlier fastball thanks to its rise and his unusual release point, and he's an interesting "ceiling" candidate in the rotation. However, his substantial history of injuries may mean he's best used out of the bullpen.

Industry observers note that the Detroit Tigers have added infield depth by agreeing to terms with Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year, $5 million free agent contract, ESPN reports. Kim, 31, is coming off a rough partial season with the Atlanta Braves, but he has a more palatable OPS+ of 91 for his career. He's been a primary shortstop in recent years and also has significant time spent at second base and third base.

Sources indicate that even after achieving a reunion with veteran starting pitcher Sonny Gray, the Minnesota Twins are still looking to fortify their roster for a return to contention in 2027. The club still hopes to make one more significant addition this offseason and add another player who may not grab as many headlines, the Athletic reports. Atop the wishlist are a first baseman or a second baseman and another lefty reliever.

According to recent reports, even after the splash addition of Skubal, the Mets may not be done adding starting pitchers in the service of a rebound season in 2027. On that front, the Mets may be interested in adding a starting pitcher on a short-term deal for next season, the Athletic reports. That would likely limit them to the back half of the market, especially with so many bigger names reaching agreements.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that welcome to the most special week in the NFL. We watched the Los Angeles Rams defeat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night, and now, we have three exciting Thanksgiving matchups to digest this "Turkey Day.".

Sources indicate that football fans suffered through many sleepy Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions Thanksgiving matchups over the years. Now, this 1 p.m. game on Thursday is expected to be one of the most exciting holiday matchups in recent memory. After that, the Dallas Cowboys will welcome Joe Milton III and the Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium. Both teams are coming off wins, and the Cowboys need this game if they want to keep pace in the NFC East. At the end of the night, we have a potential AFC Championship preview to watch when the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. This is just the second game in NFL history to feature two teams coming off at least three straight 17-point victories.

According to recent reports, which teams should you pick in Week 12, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 25 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.

Industry observers note that dajani (Bears -1.5): I can't remember being more excited for a Thanksgiving Day game, as the Bears and Lions are two of the best teams in the NFL. What I keep going back to is that the Bears are 6-0 while averaging 33.7 points in games where Caleb Williams starts and finishes. Then, factor in how much improved this Chicago defense looks with the addition of Jeffery Simmons. In Weeks 1-7, they ranked dead last in both yards per play (6.3) and yards per attempt (8.7). Over the last four weeks, the Bears now rank in the top 10 in both categories. Chicago has been swept by Detroit in each of the last two seasons. I think the Bears are done with losing to Dan Campbell …  Prediction: Bears 30, Lions 28.

Dubin (Lions +1.5): These are two incredibly evenly-matched teams, but it seems like Detroit has more matchup advantages offensively against Chicago's improved defense than the Bears do against the Lions' own improved unit. With Detroit also getting the benefit of home-field advantage, we're rolling with the Lions to win a close one as a home underdog. … Prediction: Lions 31, Bears 30.

According to recent reports, dajani (Cowboys -8.5): I don't think the Cowboys have exorcised all of their defensive demons just because they blew out the Tennessee Titans, but that win at home was just what this team needed. This is one of those cases where I think the Cowboys just simply out-score their opponent. This is still a rivalry, but the Eagles are 2-8 against the spread this season, which ranks second-worst in the NFL behind the Los Angeles Chargers, and are 0-5 against the spread in their last five divisional matchups. The Cowboys should get this cover in the fourth quarter. They have scored NINETY-ONE (91) points over the past two games! That's the most in a two-game span since 1971…  Prediction: Cowboys 33, Eagles 20.

According to recent reports, dubin (Eagles +8.5): I know they just beat the Titans by 21, but I don't like laying this many points with the Cowboys. Their defense is still too suspect and they are still too prone to games where they don't perform up to expectations for me to be comfortable with an 8.5-point spread. So even while I think they'll dent the scoreboard at home on Thanksgiving afternoon, I can't bring myself to predict that this will be a blowout. … Prediction: Cowboys 30, Eagles 24.

Dajani (Chiefs +3): The craziest part about this rivalry is that the Bills have won the last five regular-season meetings, while the Chiefs have won the last four playoff meetings! You should also know that the weather is supposed to be terrible on Thursday night, so this could come down to which team runs the ball better. James Cook has recorded nine straight games with 75 rushing yards and a touchdown. He and Josh Allen are the second duo to ever account for double-digit rushing touchdowns each through the first 10 games of a season. Meanwhile, on the other side, Emmett Johnson has rushed for 206 yards with 108 receiving yards and three touchdowns over the last two games in place of the injured Kenneth Walker III. I almost think a three-point spread in this matchup is pretty high. That's going to lead me to take the points even though Bills over Chiefs has been an auto-bet in the regular season recently… Prediction: Chiefs 17, Bills 16.

Dubin (Bills -3): I have basically the exact same analysis of this game as Dajani but come down on the opposite side of the bet because of the Bills' regular-season history against the Chiefs and the relative strength of their run game. I trust Josh Allen and James Cook to run the ball more than I do Emmett Johnson, even with how good Johnson has been over the last two weeks. Could Patrick Mahomes make this prediction look silly? Of course. But I think that'll prove more difficult in Thursday night's expected weather. … Prediction: Bills 21, Chiefs 17.

According to recent reports, dajani (Broncos -3.5): Aaron Rodgers lobbed a grenade into the Pittsburgh Steelers facility as he exited it this week. Going on national television and calling your coach a narcoleptic, unhealthy, lazy person who doesn't even know the franchise he works for is insane. So, this is a moment that will ultimately rally the locker room, or cause them to completely fall apart. Pick which side you'd like. The Steelers have also won and covered in six straight home games. This seems like an appropriate time for that streak to end   …  Prediction: Broncos 20, Steelers 13.

Dubin (Broncos -3.5): After the disaster that hit the Steelers this week, I just can't see them keeping the game close against the Broncos. No, I don't think they'll get the backup quarterback bounce from Mason Rudolph. I don't trust the Broncos as far as Bo Nix or I can throw them, but given the state the Steelers' locker room has to be in right now, I think you have to roll with Denver to cover this one with relative ease. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Steelers 10.

Recent findings suggest that dajani (Ravens +7): I have the Houston Texans winning this game, but seven points seems a bit high. C.J. Stroud is playing some great football, but his production has been overshadowed by a defense that has fallen from No. 2 in points allowed per game in 2025, to 17th this year. The Texans are 1-8 against the spread in their last nine home games following an ATS win. I'll take Baltimore to keep it close… Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 18.

Sources indicate that dubin (Ravens +7): The Ravens have now lost six straight, but they've lost the two games in the Jacoby Brissett era by a combined five points despite turning the ball over six times in those contests. If they can just limit the giveaways, I think they might even be able to pull off an upset against a Houston team that hasn't exactly lit the world on fire this year. Either way, I think they can keep it close by throwing on a surprisingly vulnerable Texans pass defense. … Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 20.

In a recent development, dajani (49ers -3): Sam Darnold is expected to return this week, and he's accounted for 10 touchdowns compared to nine interceptions in seven starts this season. If you throw out the season opener that Drew Lock finished and won, Darnold is 2-4 as a starter this season.

In a recent development, believe it or not, San Francisco is 0-9 against the spread in its last nine home divisional games. With the number at a field goal, the 49ers have a good chance to end that streak this week. What they did to the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City last Sunday night was shocking. The 49ers should be headlining everyone's NFL power rankings if they weren't already. Their 0.19 EPA per play is the best mark since the 2018 Chiefs, and they have the best offensive success rate (54.8%) by any team in a season since at least 2000 …  Prediction: 49ers 24, Seahawks 20.

Dubin (49ers -3): I reserve the right to flip this prediction to Seattle if Brock Purdy is out with his ankle injury, but if he's in, I just think that this San Francisco offense is a buzzsaw that can't really be stopped — even by the Dark Side defense. Remember, they dropped 32 points on Seattle the last time out. And they've scored 35 or more in each of their three games since returning from the bye. I don't think they can be stopped when everyone is healthy. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Seahawks 23.

Dajani (Raiders +4.5): Maybe part of me is rooting for Fernando Mendoza in his first primetime start? Last week against the Broncos, he threw for 267 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. It was a solid performance, even though the rookie was sacked five times. The Raiders certainly have their weaknesses. They are on pace to become the first team since the 2022 Texans to finish bottom two in both rushing yards per game and opponent rushing yards per game, but this 6-4 Cleveland Browns team hasn't won a game by five-plus points since LAST YEAR. That gives me some optimism Vegas can cover  …  Prediction: Browns 24, Raiders 20.

Dubin (Raiders +4.5): I will continue to stand on the idea that this Browns team is not good. Every one of Cleveland's wins has required a game-winning drive in the final minutes of the fourth quarter. The Browns have been out-gained in seven of their 10 games and are somehow 6-4. That is not remotely sustainable. I think the Raiders pull off the upset behind Fernando Mendoza and a returning Brock Bowers. … Prediction: Raiders 21, Browns 17.

Recent findings suggest that dajani (Panthers +3): I'm going to take the points with the Panthers because they are playing on the road. If you were unaware, Carolina is 3-2 away from Charlotte, and has a +8 turnover differential. The Panthers have a -4 turnover differential at home, and allow 37.4 points per game at Bank of America Stadium! For whatever reason, the Panthers are a better team on the road.

Sources indicate that it's true that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers throttled the Panthers in Week 7, 43-13, but I think Carolina splits the season series. The Buccaneers are 1-9 against the spread in their last 10 home games, and 0-7 against the spread in their last seven home primetime games. Baker Mayfield is a shocking 1-13 in primetime since 2021, so I'll back Bryce Young …  Prediction: Panthers 28, Buccaneers 27.

Dubin (Buccaneers -3): The last time these two teams played, the Bucs racked up 258 rushing yards. The Panthers' run defense then limited the Packers, Broncos and Saints over the next three games, but the Ravens hit them up for 157 yards last week. I don't see much reason to believe that the Bucs will be slowed on the ground, and I don't trust Carolina's offense to score enough to get the Bucs out of their run-heavy orientation. … Prediction: Buccaneers 20, Panthers 16.

Grading the stress levels for 76ers, Celtics, Warriors and more

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that blake Griffin told an interesting story recently, recalling playing golf with former teammate JJ Redick.
  • In a recent development, this was before Redick became the head coach of the Lakers.
  • It has been revealed that "The way I took it and the way I think that he meant it," Griffin told GQ, "is it's such a grind, mental grind, physical grind of putting literally everything you have into this thing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that blake Griffin told an interesting story recently, recalling playing golf with former teammate JJ Redick. At that point, Redick was already retired and Griffin was nearing the end of his career.

In a recent development, this was before Redick became the head coach of the Lakers. He had some perspective on his post-playing days that he offered to Griffin, something that stuck with the longtime Clipper years later. Redick told Griffin that he wouldn't be "truly happy" until he retired. Knowing how that might sound, Griffin was quick to clarify that they weren't miserable playing basketball, but rather that the two men were similar in their extensive, obsessive preparation.

It has been revealed that "The way I took it and the way I think that he meant it," Griffin told GQ, "is it's such a grind, mental grind, physical grind of putting literally everything you have into this thing. And then when you're done, you just find this fresh sense of peace.".

Sources indicate that put another way, pressure is baked into being in the NBA. The severity might vary from player to player or team to team, but it's natural enough to feel a certain amount of weight given the intensity of the competition. With that in mind, here are some estimations on current stress levels around the league.

All things considered, the Sixers have to be pretty happy with how they've started the season. Even after the Blazers snapped their five-game win streak on Monday, Philly is 14-4 and sits atop the East. LeBron James, unsurprisingly, has been a fantastic addition, particularly as a distributor and playmaker. Jaylen Brown is playing his usual heavy minutes while shooting nearly 50% from the floor. And, crucially, Joel Embiid — who missed a combined 150 games over the previous three seasons — has appeared in all but four games to date. Those are all wins for the Sixers.

In a recent development, to the extent that there's any cause for concern here, it's how sustainable all this is for them. Of the 18 games they've played, they're a perfect 12-0 in the clutch (games decided by five points or fewer with five minutes or less to go). That's tops in the NBA, and they must feel good about being at their best when things get a little dicey. But as Tyrese Maxey pointed out earlier in the season when they were starting to fall into this rhythm of playing close game after close game, he and the Sixers would prefer to stack a few victories that don't cause them to sweat right until the end.

Winning in the clutch sure beats the alternative. For now, it's less of a problem than something to monitor.

Just a couple of weeks ago, the Celtics won the battle of frenemies and were perched atop the Eastern Conference. Things haven't gone quite to strategy since then. All of a sudden, the Celtics have lost four in a row, including two one-point losses at Sacramento and Golden State. Boston handed the Kings just their second win of the season, and dropped the game to the Stephen Curry-less Warriors. Not the kind of basketball the Celtics are accustomed to playing.

Sources indicate that things haven't been easy lately for Boston. The Sacramento and Golden State games were on a back-to-back as part of a difficult, still-in-progress stretch in the schedule in which Boston plays six of seven on the road, culminating in another back-to-back when the Celtics face the Spurs in San Antonio this coming Sunday, followed by the Mavericks in Dallas on Monday.

Industry observers note that perhaps most troubling of all, two-way star Derrick White has been merely a one-way contributor for a while now. White had a disappointing shooting season a year ago. Considering his talent, the smart bet was that he would bounce back and be more efficient this season. That hasn't happened. White is shooting 41% from the floor and an abysmal 28.9% from deep. The 3-point mark is the worst of his career by a good stretch. He made just 2 of 12 from distance against the Warriors and was visibly frustrated with himself.

The Celtics have long had a theory of how they like to play: take and make more 3s than the opposition on any given night. When their shots are falling, they're tough to beat. When they aren't, anyone can knock them off. Right now, they're struggling, White in particular. Boston doesn't really have any choice but to let White try to shoot his way back into form. He's too key to their overall intends, and they'd never be able to replace his impact at the other end of the floor, where he remains one of the best all-around defenders in the league. Either he fixes his shot and Boston is back in business, or he doesn't and life at the office gets a lot tougher for everyone.

According to recent reports, when the Timberwolves revealed in October that Anthony Edwards would undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee, it took some people by surprise. Edwards looked good to start the season. He torched the Heat in the opening outing, going for 45 points and draining nine 3s. In his fourth game, on the second night of a back-to-back, he put up 47 points in a close two-point loss at Cleveland — and then suddenly and without warning, he was out of commission and expected to miss approximately two months.

Industry observers note that edwards recently said that he "never wanted to have surgery" and he felt pretty good during the offseason. He thought he was managing the knee well then, and it wasn't swollen during the summer. But after the aforementioned back-to-back, the knee "was really bad, like painful to fly. So I'm like, 'I'm gonna get [the surgery].'".

According to recent reports, without him, the Wolves have fared better than some might have expected, going a tidy 10-4. They're third in the Western Conference, trailing only the Spurs and Lakers. That should have head coach Chris Finch and the Wolves optimistic about staying afloat until Edwards returns. Except no one seems to be sure when that might be, including Edwards, who recently cast some doubt on the initial timetable when he mentioned he has "no clue" when he'll be back on the floor.

Recent findings suggest that if we go by the original estimation, two months would put Ant in late December. Now that ballpark appears far less than certain. The Wolves have performed admirably with him sidelined, but in a loaded West, Minnesota will need Edwards back sooner than "no clue" if it wants to stay near the top of the conference and especially if the Wolves hope to make a deep postseason run.

Recent findings suggest that ant is the unquestionable leader in all departments for Minnesota. In his absence, things have sometimes felt a little tense  — to the point where one noted knucklehead has periodically gotten frustrated by another. Getting Edwards back would definitely help on the court. It wouldn't hurt the vibes, either.

What are the Cavs even doing? They're 9-9 after losing to the Bulls (without Caleb Wilson, no less) on Monday. That puts them one game up on the Magic for seventh in the East. They're just 2-6 outside of Cleveland. But hey, James Harden recently went for 51 points against the Pacers and now has more 50-point games in his career than Kobe Bryant. Maybe that will console Cavs fans. Seems unlikely, though.

When you reach the conference finals, bring back your four most important players and add a fifth starter coming off a promising season, the expectations are understandably high. So far, the Cavs haven't exactly met them. Cleveland has been a top 10 offensive team, but bottom 10 in defense. That leaves them pretty much looking like what their record indicates — average at best, a team that could lose to an inferior opponent (like, say, Chicago) on any random night in November.

Recent findings suggest that it certainly hasn't helped that they've been without Evan Mobley of late. He's missed the last six games with a toe injury. Peyton Watson, the aforementioned addition to the starting lineup, hasn't been anywhere near as good in Cleveland as he was in Denver last season. All of that has left Donovan Mitchell with too much heavy lifting, and so far he hasn't been able to shoulder the load on his own. The longer this mediocrity continues, the more we're left to wonder whether the Cavs are overdue to shake up their starting unit and offload one of the big names.

[Looks around to see if anyone else is cringing] They just lost to the Pacers.

In a recent development, in fairness, no team has been hit with more major injuries than the Thunder. Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) could very well miss the remainder of the season after both underwent surgery, while Chet Holmgren (knee) is expected to miss at least three months. That's three of the team's five starters to begin the season. Not good. Except to hear the reigning back-to-back MVP tell it, there's something unexpected to be gleaned from the experience.

"Honestly speaking, it's kind of fun," Shai Gilgeous-Alexander noted last week. "We've kind of had the wind at our back the last couple of years and had our way a lot of nights, and to have that kind of adversity, it's kind of fun. I embrace it. It'll make me better.".

Recent findings suggest that SGA has a different definition of fun than most people. After losing in Indiana on Monday, the Thunder are just two games over .500, which puts them 10th in the West. [Go ahead and cringe if you weren't already doing so.].

If there's any team that can withstand SGA's bizarre version of a good time, it's the Thunder. Sam Presti assembled the deepest team in the NBA, but there are limits to what even they can handle. In the absence of several key players, Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain, Isaiah Hartenstein and others have all been tasked with picking up considerable slack. That includes rookies Aday Mara and Bennett Stirtz. When you're missing so many key pieces, you stop being deep at some point and just do your best to plug holes. Even the mighty Thunder can only do so much.

In a recent development, the Warriors snapped a five-game losing streak by beating the Celtics at home on Sunday in a white-knuckled one-point win. Alas, they only managed 88 points in the victory and the offense looked super sluggish yet again. Even with the win over Boston, the Warriors are 9-8 and 11th in the West standings. Things have gone sideways when you're looking up at everyone but the Pelicans, Clippers, Jazz and Kings.

In a recent development, the Warriors' start to the season was fun while it lasted. Yaxel Lendeborg played great — and talked just as well — and immediately cemented himself in the starting lineup, not to mention the Rookie of the Year race. Even more encouraging, Stephen Curry looked like a vintage version of himself again after playing just 43 games a season ago. Through the first 11 games this year, Curry was second in the league in scoring behind only Luka Dončić. He appeared sharp and healthy — until he came out of the game in Houston in early November while holding his side after playing just six minutes. Turned out to be an abdominal tear. The Warriors revealed that he would be reevaluated in two weeks, though the general ballpark for that kind of injury is closer to a month.

Recent findings suggest that not great, especially considering the Warriors were hardly at full strength as it was. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody have yet to play a single minute while both recover from knee injuries. Meanwhile, Kristaps Porziņģis — who signed a new two-year deal worth $40 million in the offseason — is dealing with health problems and recently stepped away from basketball. Curry is the most critical piece of all, but not having several key components has left the Warriors painfully thin. That has reminded the Warriors how much tougher life is for all of them when Curry isn't on the floor and a rookie is suddenly tasked with leading the way.

#130612. NBA Hater Report: Celtics can't shoot, neither can Trae Young and James Harden isn't close to a top 10 player

NBA Hater Report: Celtics can't shoot, neither can Trae Young and James Harden isn't close to a top 10 player

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2161 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Welcome back to the NBA Hater Report: A breakdown of some of the players, teams and trends around the league that are drawing the ire of yours truly.
  • The Celtics are hitting their first skid of the season, having lost four straight to drop to 11-6, including a demoralizing back-to-back against the now two-win Kings and the sans-Stephen Curry Warriors.
  • Lack of rim pressure was always going to be, and has long been, an obstacle for the Celtics, who are averaging just 47 drives per game (third-fewest in the league).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Welcome back to the NBA Hater Report: A breakdown of some of the players, teams and trends around the league that are drawing the ire of yours truly. If you're not a fellow pessimist, proceed with caution.

The Celtics are hitting their first skid of the season, having lost four straight to drop to 11-6, including a demoralizing back-to-back against the now two-win Kings and the sans-Stephen Curry Warriors. They failed to hit 100 points against the Kings and their 28th-ranked defense. They managed just 87 at Golden State.

Lack of rim pressure was always going to be, and has long been, an obstacle for the Celtics, who are averaging just 47 drives per game (third-fewest in the league). Only 25.6% of their shots are at the rim, the fourth-fewest in the league per Cleaning the Glass, and no team takes fewer shots per game from inside the restricted area.

They are about as extreme a jump-shooting team as you will find, and right now the shots are not going in. Over these last four, the Celtics have made just 28% of their 3s and 38% of their overall shots. Throw in 65% from the free-throw line and those are all bottom-two marks over that span, plus the 389 points they scored is the lowest over any four-game stretch since 2012 for a Boston offense.

In a recent development, it's not just the number of 3s the Celtics rely, sometimes more than others, it's the kinds of 3s. Every team wants the shots off ball and player movement, drives and kicks, drawing two and swinging, but when the Celtics aren't able to create the initial leverage by attacking the rim (they don't have to do this with just drives; they aim to do so by cutting and rolling, too), they end up taking more pull-up 3s than any team in the league, both as a total number and percentage of their overall shot diet.

Those are traditionally tougher shots, and indeed Boston is making them at a 33.5% clip. The Celtics also don't generate a ton of the coveted corner 3s (which are often a result of rim pressure) relative to their volume, and thus take more above-the-break 3s than any team. There are also a lot of one-on-one 3s; only the Lakers and Timberwolves take more 3s after three or more dribbles, and the Celtics make those at only 29%.

Sources indicate that bottom line, Derrick White is shooting 28% from 3 for the year and has missed 22 of his last 25 from deep (he had so many premium looks against Golden State and they just will not go in for him). Payton Pritchard has missed 21 of his last 29 from deep. Jayson Tatum is having a stellar all-around season and is leveraging his scoring attention to find teammates more effectively than ever, but quietly his shooting is in the dumps, too.

In a recent development, tatum is shooting 42.6% overall and 33.6% from 3, both of which would be career lows if you discard the 15 games he played last season after returning ahead of schedule from the Achilles tear. Tatum has never been a particularly adept pull-up 3-point shooter, for which he'll probably always be prone to settling to at least some degree. Tatum's pull-up 3s over his last four full seasons:.

It has been revealed that any team that launches as many 3s as the Celtics is going to endure some extreme ebbs and flows, and coach Joe Mazzulla remains committed to the course. "... If we're getting good shots, which more times than not we are, you have to be able to trust over the course of a season that that's going to work out," he noted.

In a recent development, the truth is, the Celtics don't really have a choice other than to trust the shots to go in. They don't have a proposal B to speak of. They don't get to the rim and they don't have a post presence. They have a gang of good shooters, but that doesn't guarantee good shooting.

Industry observers note that the Celtics rely on getting more shots than their opponents by winning the turnover and offensive-rebounding battles, which they generally do, but as Mazzulla also mentioned, "at some point you have to knock [the shots] down. That's just not happening right now.".

After Harden scored 51 against the Pacers last Friday, Cleveland coach Kenny Atkinson did the increasingly cliché "we've got to appreciate this guy" dance while calling Harden a "top 10 of all-time" player.

It has been revealed that kenny Atkinson after James Harden's 51-point game: "We've got to appreciate this guy. This guy is top 10 of all-time." pic.twitter.com/YUt2Y6pQYL.

It has been revealed that remember, Atkinson is the guy who told reporters: "Analytically … we've won two out of three" right before the Cavaliers got swept by the Knicks in last year's Eastern Conference Finals. That was kind of overblown, to be fair. He was simply citing the types of shots the Cavs got vs. the ones the Knicks got, and that getting the right shots is a recipe for success more often than not, which every coach from the beginning of time has believed.

According to recent reports, atkinson just would've been better off if he'd gone the "make or miss league" route. Once you start invoking analytical results over actual results, you're going to get rightfully roasted as the number nerd that you are.

In a recent development, through this lens, it makes sense that Atkinson thinks Harden is a top 10 all-time player. Numbers-wise, he's ninth all-time with almost 30,000 career points. He's 11th in assists and, barring injury, will almost surely pass Isiah Thomas for 10th by the end of the season. Only Stephen Curry has made more 3-pointers than Harden, who's piled up so many numbers he's actually top 20 all-time in steals.

None of this adds up to top 10.

Of course this is subjective, but this is my Hater Report, so allow me to hate. Harden was a manipulating machine of egregious proportions. I'm not saying he wasn't a great scorer, or even that he sometimes still isn't. Two things can indeed be true. But if we're going to start throwing around top 10, we're sure as hell going to factor heavily the conditions under which you dominated.

Sources indicate that harden played in the NBA's version of the steroid era. It was juiced up on some level for every scorer, but nobody mastered the dark arts like Harden, who cheated his way to so many phony fouls that guys were literally starting to guard him with their hands behind their backs.

According to recent reports, now listen, before you start with the "he wasn't breaking any rules" nonsense, keep in mind that steroids weren't technically illegal in baseball when Barry Bonds' head looked like it was going to pop. Harden scammed his way to more points than anyone in history. The flops and flails were impossible to stomach or, more importantly, defend against. Falling down on damn near every 3-pointer he took actually became part of his follow-through. I would only be mildly surprised if you hid a camera in his private workouts if he wasn't falling down in an empty gym, because he was so used to doing it.

This created more than just a gazillion free throws; it created a scoring environment in which Harden could operate against defenders who were way more frightened of fouling than being scored on. It was as if he was being perpetually defended by guys with five fouls.

Recent findings suggest that now account for the one-man-show usage. I remember Raja Bell once telling me there are way more players than you think who could score 25 points per game if given the opportunity. Hell, Darius Acuff Jr. is doing it right now and until a week ago, he was a teenager.

Recent findings suggest that that's not to say anyone could do what Harden did, but given his set of circumstances, it's irresponsible to call him one of the 10 greatest players ever on numbers alone. Back in 2022, ESPN ranked him 50th all time, which feels much closer to reality, and he's only gotten worse since then.

I mean, just start rattling names off the top of your head. Michael Jordan, LeBron James, Stephen Curry, Kevin Durant, Wilt Chamberlain, Larry Bird, Magic Johnson, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Hakeem Olajuwon, Kobe Bryant, Tim Duncan, Shaquille O'Neal. We're already at 12 and there's not even a debate with any of them.

No coach in his right mind would take Harden over Nikola Jokić, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Kevin Garnett, Karl Malone, Scottie Pippen, Charles Barkley, Isiah Thomas, Dwyane Wade or prime Chris Paul. I never watched Oscar Robertson, Jerry West, Julius Erving, Moses Malone, Elgin Baylor or some guy named Bill Russell, but something tells me the vast majority of coaches are taking those guys over Harden, too.

It bears repeating that none of this means to suggest Harden hasn't been an all-time player. He's a first-ballot Hall of Famer. He's not an empty-stats guy by any stretch; he led a team that very possibly would've won the championship in the middle of Golden State's dynasty were it not for a Chris Paul injury. But there are levels to this, and trying to elevate Harden into the top one on the strength of gaudy numbers in an absolutely juiced-up era of his game would be like trying to call Sammy Sosa one of the greatest hitters ever. It's just not even close to true.

In a recent development, back in 2021, I called Young an average shooter who thinks he's Stephen Curry and got absolutely roasted for it. Turns out, I wasn't harsh enough on Young, whose shooting has been consistently deteriorating to the point that he is now a flat-out bad shooter. Even with a 7-for-15 run from 3 over his last two games, which at this point is a downright nuclear stretch for him, Young is shooting 32.5% from 3 and a pitiful 36.4% overall.

According to recent reports, the fact that he's among the league leaders in assists means almost nothing; passing has always been his one elite gift (it goes largely hand in hand with his former ability to breach the paint at will), but it comes at the hefty cost of him controlling the ball for almost the same amount of time per possession as Luka Dončić this season. Just because those two were traded for one another doesn't mean they are, or ever have been, anywhere near the same caliber of player.

Sources indicate that even at his peak when he was one of the league's better shot generators, it was debatable whether you could justify sponsoring Young's personal dribbling show with your offense, let alone paying him max money given the defensive trade-off. But now that he can't shoot or beat anyone off the dribble, that $212 million deal the Wizards gifted him this summer, which was a disaster the moment the ink dried, somehow looks even worse.

It has been revealed that washington is trying to salvage some sort of value from Young. They're starting to take him off the ball some, which, given the good shooting the last few games, is going to give the apologists hope. Don't fall for it. The numbers, not just this year but going back a long time, speak for themselves.

There's a difference between a talented shooter and a good one. Young fooled people with range and confidence for a while, and he had an unearned marksman reputation that died hard. But the jig is up. This is an average shooter at best, and he's rarely at his best.

After losing four straight games by 20-plus while also being held under 100 points in each (an equation of futility that goes unmatched by any other team this century), the Warriors finally got their first win since losing Curry to an oblique tear by beating the aforementioned ice-cold Celtics.

It certainly wasn't because of their offense. The Warriors were once again held to double digits, managing just 88 points. Over this five-game stretch, the Warriors, who register a top-five offense with Curry, have scraped together an anemic 96.2 points per 100 possessions on 48.5% true-shooting, both being the worst marks in the league by a laughable margin.

Industry observers note that over this five-game stretch, the Warriors have been outscored by 108 points. The 1997-98 team that also lost four straight by at least 20 points was a minus-104 over that stretch. That was the season that Latrell Sprewell choked P.J. Carlesimo, mind you. The Warriors won 19 games. That's the kind of company these Warriors are trolling in right now.

If Curry doesn't get back soon, we might have to start worrying about Draymond Green putting Steve Kerr in a full nelson.
