#130580. What all 30 MLB teams have to be thankful for this year

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (2938 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

What all 30 MLB teams have to be thankful for this year

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2938 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that happy Thanksgiving, baseball enthusiasts!
  • Industry observers note that on this Thanksgiving holiday, here is one thing fans of each MLB team can be thankful for this year.
  • In a recent development, the Diamondbacks have been tantalizingly close to the playoffs the last two years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that happy Thanksgiving, baseball enthusiasts! As the holiday name suggests, Thursday is a day to be grateful for the good things that have happened and the good things to come. Non-football sports are often secondary on Turkey Day, but baseball is a way of life as much as it is an interest. It's a companion, there with you every night during the summer.

Industry observers note that on this Thanksgiving holiday, here is one thing fans of each MLB team can be thankful for this year. Mike Axisa handled the American League and Dayn Perry tackled the National League. Now sit back, loosen up your belt, and take a gander as you digest.

In a recent development, the Diamondbacks have been tantalizingly close to the playoffs the last two years. Know what might get them over the hump in 2027? The return of Corbin Burnes. Their on-paper ace returned from Tommy John surgery in time to make three subpar starts this past season, but his true comeback – one that brings with it the hope of a return to peak form – will come next season. Assuming all goes well, Burnes will be a huge boon to the Snakes' hopes in 2027.

In a recent development, on the field, 2026 went about as poorly as possible for the Athletics. Almost every core player missed significant time with injury and their pitching was wretched. At a time when the A's are supposed to be building up for their move to Las Vegas, they went from 76 wins in 2025 to 64 wins in 2026. Yeesh. The good news is the A's have newly introduced leadership. President of baseball operations Taylor Smith comes over from the Red Sox and general manager Cam Castro joins from the Brewers, which are two pretty good teams to emulate. The Athletics needed new voices and a fresh perspective in the front office, and they have it now.

Industry observers note that for the Braves, their gratitude comes from reflection. Last season, they rebounded from the disappointments of 2025 to log 94 wins and claim the National League East title. As well, they won a postseason series for the first time since 2021. On top of that, the Braves exacted revenge upon their NL East rivals, the Phillies, by defeating them in the Wild Card Series. That comes after the Phillies eliminated the Braves in 2022 and 2023.

Recent findings suggest that the Orioles again failed to reach the postseason this past season and they traded away Adley Rutschman, once the face of the franchise, at the deadline. It was a disappointing year through and through. Year 1 of the Pete Alonso experience certainly went well, though. He led all first basemen with 5.0 WAR, led the league with 43 home runs and 113 RBI, and finished fifth in the AL MVP voting. Right-handed power is in shockingly short supply these days and the O's have one of the very best right-handed power hitters in their game anchoring their lineup. Big money free agent signings should all work out as well as Alonso did in 2026.

It has been revealed that there is a lot to like about the Red Sox at the major-league level. They've added Jake Bauers, Curtis Mead, and Adley Rutschman to their lineup in the last four months or so, and the rotation is stacked with Jake Bennett, Garrett Crochet, Ranger Suárez, and Payton Tolle. Boston also has one of the very best prospects in the game knocking on the door in Franklin Arias. The shortstop of the future (and, very soon, the present) slashed .323/.400/.557 with 25 home runs and only 74 strikeouts in 117 games between Double-A and Triple-A in 2027. Not-so-bold prediction: Arias will be the Red Sox's Opening Day shortstop next year.

The Cubs are very much in contending mode right now, even if their last two trips to the postseason haven't yielded anything close to the desired results. The foundation, though, is there, and it's Pete Crow-Armstrong. Not only is he one of the best all-around and most electric performers in the games, but he's also just 24 years of age. Best of all, at least from the Cubs' standpoint, he's under contract through 2032 at what will almost certainly turn out to be deep-bargain rates.

According to recent reports, here is the complete list of right-handed hitters to hit 30 home runs, walk 100 times, and strike out fewer than 130 times since the 2020 pandemic season: Miguel Vargas in 2026. That's it. The last righty hitters to do it before Vargas were Alex Bregman and Mike Trout in 2019. Munetaka Murakami may have gotten the headlines, but Vargas was the White Sox's best player this year. He's a legitimate star with a special blend of contact, power, and plate discipline. Getting Vargas for spare parts (Erick Fedde, Michael Kopech, Tommy Pham) at the 2025 trade deadline has proven to be a terrific move by POBO Chris Getz.

Industry observers note that the Reds are a bit rudderless right now, but their rooters can be grateful that sparkling shortstop Elly De La Cruz is on the roster. With a 30-30 season and a breakout campaign with the bat freshly behind him, De La Cruz is poised to become an MVP candidate as a 25-year-old in 2027. Whether that's with Cincy long-term or as a blockbuster trade piece that nets the Reds a true haul remains to be determined.

Recent findings suggest that it has never been a question of talent with Chase DeLauter. He had just been held back by injuries, most notably a series of foot injuries, dating back to his time at James Madison. This year, though, DeLauter stayed on the field and turned in an excellent rookie season: .287/.363/.457 with 16 home runs and only 82 strikeouts in 133 games. The underlying data (exit velocity, etc.) is impressive. Once DeLauter learns how to pull a few more balls in the air rather than push them the other way, he'll be a monster. The Guardians are in perpetual need of offense and DeLauter looks like a long-term keeper in the middle of the lineup.

Rare is the primary catcher who tops 40 home runs in a season, but that's exactly what Hunter Goodman did in 2026. That makes him a hugely valuable presence moving forward. Whether that's as a Rockie as the modernized front office gets them up to speed or as a blockbuster trade target for other teams is TBD. Either way, he's a needle-mover. For those curious, 25 of his 41 home runs last season came away from Coors Field.

It has been revealed that it ultimately did not happen, but as late as August, Kevin McGonigle had a chance to finish with the third-highest WAR by a rookie position player in the Expansion Era (since 1961), behind only Mike Trout and Aaron Judge. Even without that admittedly obscure distinction, McGonigle was sensational in 2026, slashing .278/.376/.430 with 18 home runs and nearly as many walks (95) as strikeouts (100). He won American League Rookie of the Year and finished seventh in the AL MVP voting. Best of all, the Tigers wisely locked McGonigle up to an eight-year, $150 million extension in April. That will keep him in Detroit through 2034 and it already looks like a bargain.

I don't think there's a better or more imposing hitter in baseball than Yordan Alvarez. He's so big and scary! Years of near-MLB-best performance finally culminated in an AL MVP award this season as Air Yordan slashed .316/.432/.601 with 42 home runs and nearly as many walks (109) as strikeouts (120). Here's something that flew under the radar: Alvarez was intentionally walked 33 times, second most in American League history behind Aaron Judge's 36 in 2025. You know you're good when teams put you on intentionally that much. The Astros eked out an AL West title this past season and Alvarez was the single biggest reason.

Bobby Witt Jr. turned in another terrific season and finished second among all players with 7.0 WAR. He's a given here. Now he has a great running mate in Jac Caglianone, who reined in the swing-and-miss and slashed .289/.340/.494 with 23 home runs. His exit velocity and hard-hit data are among the very best in baseball. All Caglianone needs to do to become one of the game's truly elite hitters is reduce his ground ball rate, which was an elevated 46.3% in 2026. You'd like to see that number down around 38% (if not lower) for a guy with this much power. Point is, the Royals have a second building block in their lineup.

The Arte Moreno Reign of Error is over. Moreno has agreed to sell the Angels to Stan Kroenke for the tidy sum of $4 billion, and, if nothing else, it really can't get any worse. I mean, the Halos lost 100 games for the first time in franchise history in 2026. Kroenke's other franchises have all won a title recently (Arsenal F.C. in the English Premier League, the NBA's Denver Nuggets, the NHL's Colorado Avalanche, etc.) and tend to be smart, well-run organizations. It will take some time to turn the Angels around, but at least now there's some hope. Under Moreno, there wasn't.

The Dodgers have plenty of veteran star power on the roster, fronted of course by Shohei Ohtani. Now, though, they have some young upside on the way in outfielder Josue De Paula, who's one of the top prospects in all of baseball. The 21-year-old lefty batsman has star upside at the plate, and coming off a highly successful cuppa coffee in 2026, he's poised for a bigger role and maybe Rookie of the Year honors in 2027.

As the Marlins methodically work their way back toward relevance, Otto Lopez has emerged as A Dude. Over the last three seasons, the shortstop has increased his WAR from 2.8 in 2024 to 3.6 in 2025 to last season's mark of 6.1. Going into his age-28 season, Lopez is operating at peak and may be the most underrated player in baseball right now.

This one's not challenging. The Brewers are fresh off the first World Series title in franchise history, and those credentials are burnished by a 2026 regular season that saw them post the best record and best run differential in all of baseball. It's not "just" a championship; it's dominance en route to that championship. Fans of the Crew should thus be the most grateful of all right about now.

Industry observers note that this month was pleasantly surprising and productive for the Twins. First, Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer, and I'm not sure anyone expected that. Getting him back on a one-year contract is a win even if it is a significant salary. And second, Sonny Gray returned to Minnesota on a two-year deal worth $55 million (with an opt out). Just like that, the Twins welcomed back a key middle-of-the-order hitter and stalwart catcher, and upgraded their rotation significantly. This past season was a major disappointment, for sure, but I don't think you need to try all that hard to see this team contending for the AL Central title in 2027.

In a recent development, mets fans, your team just signed far and away the top free agent on the market in ace and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. Yes, the cost was high, but the Mets now have at the front of the rotation perhaps the best pitcher in all of baseball. The pressure is on both team and player, but the pairing is made to order for a team that needed such a presence on the staff.

I'm partial to Ron Guidry's 1978, but the case can be made that Cam Schlittler just turned in the greatest pitching season in Yankees history once you adjust for era. His 215 ERA+ is in fact a franchise record for a qualified pitcher, besting Guidry's 208 ERA+ during that 1978 season. Regardless of where Schlittler's Cy Young campaign ranks historically, he emerged as a bona fide ace in his first full MLB season, one in which he proved himself to be a Red Sox killer (always a plus for a Yankee). The Yankees turned a seventh-round draft pick into a front-of-the-rotation starter. If you can't be thankful about that, what can you?

Sources indicate that the Phillies are finally willing to move the defensively deficient Trea Turner off of shortstop. That's a welcome development. Speaking of welcome developments, veteran shortstop Corey Seager of the Texas Rangers is reportedly willing to waive his no-trade clause to join the Phils. That would be a great targeted strike by Dave Dombrowski and help keep Philly's contending window open a bit longer. And even if not, at least they're trying.

Sources indicate that shortstop Konnor Griffin held his own as a 20-year-old rookie last season, putting up a 2.1 WAR in just 80 games. It's rare enough to even reach the majors at such an age, let alone provide value. Griffin looks like a regular All-Star selection and occasional MVP candidate for years and years to come, and the Pirates have secured his services through the 2034 season.

Recent findings suggest that it's about the future in St. Louis. Under lead operator Chaim Bloom and the built-out player-development program, the Cardinals in short order have gone from a mediocre farm system to one of the very best in the game. Pair those incoming talents with in-place youngsters like JJ Wetherholt and Jordan Walker, and the future for the Cardinals is shimmering.

There's no replacing the late Peter Seidler, the beloved Padres owner who distinguished himself by caring about and committing to winning more than almost any other owner in the game. Now, though, newly introduced owners José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones have signaled they, too, have bold intentions with the Padres. They were seriously in the bidding for Tarik Skubal, and while they didn't land the top free agent, their presence in the fray suggests payroll retrenchment isn't on the way in San Diego. That's encouraging.

The Giants seem forever in need of offense lately, and rookie Bryce Eldridge in 2026 gave them value in the present and promise for the future. One of the top offensive prospects in baseball coming into 2026, he proved himself and then some after arriving in San Fran to put up a 133 OPS+ in 107 games. That was good for seventh place in the National League Rookie of the Year vote. He's looking like a middle-of-the-order presence for years to come, and that's just what this flagging organization needs.

Gosh, what a disappointing season for the Mariners. They went from Game 7 of the ALCS in 2025 -- five outs away from their first pennant! -- to 76 wins and failing to reach the postseason in the sad sack American League in 2026. Woof. On the bright side, Kade Anderson, the No. 3 pick in the 2025 Draft, promptly emerged as baseball's top pitching prospect and made seven solid major league starts late in the season. His minor-league performance was simply incredible: 1.06 ERA with 135 strikeouts and only 13 walks in 93 ⅓ Double-A innings. Anderson's emergence allowed the Mariners to trade Bryce Miller for Maikel Garcia, a trade I loved for Seattle.

Tobias Myers for Junior Caminero in November 2021 is already one of the most lopsided, landscape-altering trades of the generation, and Caminero has only played two full seasons. He hit 40-plus home runs in those two seasons, joining Hall of Famer Eddie Mathews as the only players in history to hit 40 homers twice before their age-23 season. Caminero is one of the very best hitters in the game and the Rays stole him away from the Guardians for a depth arm in Myers, who never threw a single pitch for Cleveland. A heist of seismic proportions.

If not for February UCL surgery, top prospect Sebastian Walcott likely would have made his MLB debut this summer. He returned to the field in mid-July and didn't miss a beat: .325/.401/.590 with 10 home runs in 41 minor-league games while reaching Triple-A. Walcott mashed in another 16 games in the Arizona Fall League as well. The UCL surgery was a tough break, but Walcott had a smooth recovery and will soon join a Rangers team that needs all the offensive help it can get after finishing 25th in runs in 2026.

In a recent development, I could go with something cheeky like "2026 is over (especially for Vladimir Guerrero Jr.)," but nah, we'll instead give Dylan Cease and Kazuma Okamoto their flowers for tremendous first seasons with the Blue Jays. Cease had the league's highest strikeout rate and finished second in the Cy Young voting in Year 1 of his seven-year, $210 million contract. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

Lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could. Sobbing and desolate under a cloudless Upcoming Jersey sky, he understood that his last game for Argentina had also been among his worst.

Where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl. No wonder he stood apart while Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina did their worst, preferring to absorb one more chorus of adoration from the blue-and-white disciples before forsaking the stage for good.

You could make the case that Messi, as captain of an unholy rabble that had sought only to kick lumps out of Spain, should have taken a moral lead by hauling his team-mates into line, rather than reducing himself to their level by agitating to have Marc Cucurella sent off.

Recent findings suggest that and yet for 20 years, the little sorcerer stayed aloof from his nation’s most lurid antics on the pitch, establishing himself as a strangely beatific presence on whom the highest ideals could be projected. Anybody who has heard Messi’s name being chanted by 50,000 fervent Argentines would have felt it. He was as close as 21st-century sport has come to a secular deity, the object of such veneration that Pope Francis felt compelled to remind Catholics that it was sacrilegious to keep calling him God.

Recent findings suggest that today, with one agonised announcement, that glorious delirium is over, and already Argentina seems not to know what to do with itself. Pablo Giralt, a sports anchor in Buenos Aires, was unable even to speak when he heard the news live on air, while shattered young fans described how they had called their parents in tears.

Everybody had known the moment was approaching, given the finality of his exit from the final and the subsequent death of his father, Jorge, but it still triggered an unbearable sense of loss.

Recent findings suggest that messi was the force who galvanised a nation, propelling his side from the unfathomable low of defeat to Saudi Arabia at the 2022 World Cup to holding the trophy aloft 26 days later. Who could ever hope to emulate him, to detonate such joy that the team’s homecoming bus parade in the capital had to be abandoned for a helicopter ride because of the millions on the streets?

Recent findings suggest that “Thank you, God, for making me Argentine,” Messi wrote in his earnest sign-off, his strength of allegiance unfailing to the end. As a veteran of 207 international matches, with his last at La Bombonera distinguished by an ecstatic ovation, he understood both the passions he unleashed among his people and the extent to which his own story became that of an entire country.

You struggled to imagine what life was like in the eye of this madness, with his every move stalked. For the wonder of Messi was that the cult went beyond borders, that the joy he inspired across six World Cups made him beloved to billions. An abiding memory of the 2022 final is of the walk back to the metro station in Doha, where thousands of Nepalese and Bangladeshi supporters, all part of the vast migrant workforce that had built the stadiums, united in “Messi, Messi” refrains even at 1am.

According to recent reports, messi was majestic at that tournament, so imperious in filleting Croatia in the semi-finals that Argentina’s TV reporters abandoned even the pretence of objectivity. “Truly, you made your mark in everyone’s life, and that to me is beyond winning any World Cup,” gushed Sofia Martinez of Television Publica. And when he won it all, the mark only deepened. To occupy any press box at the World Cup where Argentina were involved this summer was to see South American colleagues in “Messi 10” jerseys, helplessly in thrall to his greatness.

Recent findings suggest that as a 39-year-old, he confounded every expectation, scoring a hat-trick against Algeria and breaking Miroslav Klose’s World Cup goals record. Even when engineering those implausible fightbacks against Egypt and England, he held a volatile team together with a minimum of fuss.

Lionel Messi: #FIFAWorldCup edition 🇦🇷🌟 pic.twitter.com/E2xOh3Iose.

To study Messi at his last World Cup was to see a man spared the obligation to do anything off the ball. For large periods of each game, the most minutely scrutinised athlete on the planet would do little besides wander around, only to ignite when it mattered most. You saw it in the fateful semi-final with England, where, at 1-0 down, he sloped off to the right touchline as if absent-mindedly gardening. Except he was plotting his opponents’ downfall, working out the precise spots from which to unleash two sumptuous crosses and shatter English hearts.

That alchemy would elude him in the final, where Argentina’s bid for immortality brought only instant notoriety, not to mention £236,000 in fines for misconduct. Was Messi’s image hurt by his connection to the chaos? Not in the long run. Nobody likes to cling to the fact that Pelé’s swansong for Brazil was a drawn friendly with Yugoslavia, or that Diego Maradona bowed out of World Cup football by failing a drug test for ephedrine. What endure are the indelible masterpieces those players bequeathed en route.

It will be the same for Messi, a genius defined less by his ending than by the electrifying adrenalin rush he produced along the way, spanning three finals, 21 goals, and countless flourishes to take the breath away. “Thank you” was all he had left to say. And yet the gratitude, ultimately, is all ours.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • England wins the U21 European Championship final against Germany 3-2.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

von Next Generation am 06.07.2025 in den Kategorien National Teams mit 1 Kommentar.

England wins the U21 European Championship final against Germany 3-2. After just 20 minutes, England leads 2-0. This aspect analysis focuses on the reasons behind the German attacking press’s lack of access to England’s build-up play.

The U21 European Championship final offered several interesting tactical elements. This analysis focuses on Germany’s lack of access in their attacking pressing and marking. Particularly in the first half, England repeatedly managed to bypass the German press, often gaining large amounts of space in the final third, which led to dangerous scoring opportunities.

Industry observers note that the early deficit also contributed to Germany being unable to focus, as they usually do, on securing depth in their pressing. Instead, they were forced to put direct pressure on the ball carrier in order to force turnovers. After the equalizer to make it 2-2, Germany noticeably pressed high less frequently. Therefore, this analysis examines Germany’s pressing and marking, as well as England’s build-up play, up to the 60th minute.

One of the trends at the U21 European Championship was that many teams aimed to press the opponent’s goal kicks with a +1 player on the last line or in the space between the lines just in front of the back line. Many teams—including Germany—used man-oriented marking when closing down during goal kicks.

Since most teams build up from a 1-4-2-4 structure on goal kicks, it is equally common to press man-to-man from a 4-1-3-2 shape, with the two holding midfielders (the “sixes”) staggered vertically.

According to recent reports, the deeper-lying holding midfielder (for Germany: Martel) acts as the +1 player, positioning himself in space based on the location of the ball. When the opponent plays through the space between the lines, he can create a numerical advantage there. In the final third, pressing is carried out against a 1-4-2 build-up using a 3-2 shape. The more advanced holding midfielder (for Germany: Reitz) typically positions himself centrally and marks the ball-near holding midfielder, while the far-side winger presses the ball-far holding midfielder.

In a recent development, the English side, by contrast, caused problems for the German team’s marking assignments through an asymmetrical structure. As a result, England had several options for exploiting their numerical superiority in the build-up without having to immediately play into the space between the lines.

What remained consistent was the intention to establish central possession in front of the first pressing line using different players, in order to build up play on either side. Central possession makes it more difficult for the pressing team to steer the play in a specific direction, as the passing angles from central areas are wider than those from more advanced or wider positions.

Sources indicate that central possession complicates the opponent’s shaping of play. Anderson’s drop frees him from Woltemade’s marking shadow and creates a numerical advantage against Nebel, who must now cover both the advanced full-back and Anderson.

The asymmetry in England’s build-up play also allowed them to repeatedly exploit their numerical superiority in specific areas tailored to Germany’s pressing structure. By stretching the positioning of their two holding midfielders (the “sixes”), Reitz was forced to cover too much ground to mark both or to shift promptly to the ball-near midfielder.

Because Germany, for the reasons mentioned above, struggled to steer the press in a specific direction, Reitz was also unable to position himself closer to the ball-near player during goal kicks. Instead, he was forced to choose which of the two midfielders to mark man-to-man.

In a recent development, the wide, asymmetric positioning of the holding midfielders and advanced full-backs makes both midfielders available for passes, forcing Reitz to choose whom to mark. German forwards can’t shadow the opposing midfielders, while German wingers must decide between marking the spaced-out midfielders or full-backs.

England’s positional rotations during build-up play after goal kicks were most often initiated by holding midfielder Anderson. When Germany applied pressure (as shown in the diagram above), Anderson would frequently drop into the right half-space, almost into a right-sided centre-back position, while fellow holding midfielder Scott positioned himself more centrally, and No. 10 McAtee dropped into the higher left half-space.

According to recent reports, when Anderson instead dropped centrally in front of the goalkeeper, the right centre-back would shift wide, which in turn affected the positioning of other central players and full-backs. The specific rotations of the key players, including their reference points and triggers, are discussed in more detail in the section on England’s build-up against Germany’s high pressing.

Sources indicate that A key aspect of England’s build-up against Germany’s pressing was their ability to evade pressure through these rotations. Since Germany used man-oriented marking, they followed the English players during these movements, which repeatedly opened up spaces that England could then exploit. For example, when McAtee dropped deep into the far-side half-space, it pulled Martel—who was defending space-oriented in the center—out of position.

The aim was to repeatedly open up central areas by drawing German players out of the middle. When the full-backs, due to the rotations, were positioned deep and wide in possession, the ball-near holding midfielder would shift outward, thereby opening the central channel. This would often be followed by an overlapping run by the full-back into the half-space, allowing him to be found deep in the center with his marker behind him and plenty of space to operate.

Luring central players out of position and opening up space through rotations is one of the core principles of England’s build-up play. It significantly disrupted Germany’s ability to gain access through their man-marking approach during pressing.

Holding midfielder Anderson’s run outward opens the center, which can then be exploited by the full-back’s typical forward run.

England also added flexibility by repeatedly using long balls from their build-up play. Especially when both the full-backs and the holding midfielders were positioned deep, they opted for long passes as soon as Germany’s wingers and central players were lured far enough out. The 2–0 goal resulted from one such long ball, which was held up by striker Stansfield and laid off to the advancing Elliott and McAtee in the half-space, who now had plenty of room to operate in the open central area.

Although these long balls weren’t always as successful as in the lead-up to the 2–0, they had the effect of preventing Germany from pressing too aggressively, as players had to remain ready to cover depth in case of another long ball. For example, Martel pushed forward only hesitantly toward the dropping No. 10 McAtee, giving him significantly more time on the ball in central areas.

Against man-oriented marking systems, it is particularly important to apply intense pressure on the ball carrier, since progression is otherwise easier than against a zonal setup.

Recent findings suggest that as described, England repeatedly managed to exploit their numerical advantage in the build-up. However, Germany’s pressing approach also contributed to their lack of access. The primary aim of Germany’s pressing when closing down is less about disrupting the build-up itself, and more about winning the ball in a way that immediately creates a transition opportunity.

To do so, Germany tries to use its forwards to immediately block passing lanes to the flanks, forcing the play through the third man or central passes.

Recovering possession through intercepting a pass has the advantage over winning a tackle in that it tends to allow better control of the ball and therefore more often leads to a transition opportunity. Additionally, central ball recoveries naturally result in a shorter route to goal and, statistically, in higher-quality chances in front of goal.

However, this type of pressing also means less pressure is placed on the ball carrier, since the focus is on directing play and winning the ball after a pass. As a result, England’s ball carriers had more time to locate the free +1 player, made available through asymmetry and rotations.

Recent findings suggest that in hindsight, it might have been more effective to place greater emphasis on actively disrupting the build-up itself, because England repeatedly managed to bypass the German press dangerously. At the same time, Germany had the ability to control the game through their own possession, so it wasn’t absolutely necessary to rely on winning the ball high up the pitch to create chances.

Sources indicate that germany’s attacking pressing operated on principles similar to those of their closing down (Zustellen). From a 4-4-2 formation with a slightly advanced Reitz on the left half-space, the forwards aimed to channel the opponent’s build-up play out wide in order to isolate the wide build-up players and engage them in man-to-man marking.

Recent findings suggest that on the last defensive line, Germany aimed to maintain a +1 numerical advantage, which is why the far-side holding midfielder was usually responsible for covering depth. The German wingers were expected to track back from the full-backs to press the half-backs in the three-man defensive line that frequently formed.

The exemplary German attacking press.

Even when applying attacking pressing from open play, Germany was rarely able to gain effective access to England’s build-up. This was primarily due to England’s positional play during build-up. England’s main objective in possession is to lure opponents out of position and then exploit the spaces that open up. This goal is achieved through positional rotations that make it especially difficult for the opponent to apply effective pressure on the ball carrier during pressing. The frequency of these rotations strongly resembles the rotation-heavy positional play famously associated with Paris Saint-Germain.

The following outlines the key running paths, rotations, and reference points of the most vital players.

Sources indicate that the center-backs were rarely involved in the rotations. Only when one of the holding midfielders dropped into the build-up line did the center-backs position themselves wider. Likewise, striker Stansfield provided a fixed presence in the central deep-lying position.

Most rotations initially originated from the holding midfielders, particularly Anderson. Most frequently, he dropped into the right half-space just ahead of the center-backs. This caused the right full-back to position wider and winger Elliott to drop deeper into the half-space at the level of the last defensive line. As a result, Woltemade and Nebel had to press two players, creating a 3 vs. 2 overload.

There were also occasions when Anderson dropped into the central center-back position. Consequently, the full-backs rotated into the half-spaces, or No. 10 McAtee dropped deeper. Notably, Anderson could be found almost anywhere on the pitch. At times, he overloaded the far side, which was then followed by a role swap between him and holding midfielder Scott.

In a recent development, holding midfielder Scott often positioned himself in spaces that were left vacant after a sequence of rotations. Usually, Scott remained central or rotated roles with holding midfielder Anderson. It also happened that Scott took up an open full-back position when both the winger and the full-back rotated deep.

Sources indicate that A particularly noticeable tendency of both holding midfielders was that, when in possession, they rotated toward the flank if a wide player was positioned close to the first build-up line, making themselves available along the sideline. This had the advantage of stretching the center even further.

This was especially important because England frequently won second balls after losing possession in build-up play. In the resulting transition situation, the central area was completely free, leading to several dangerous counter-attacks through the now open middle of the pitch.

Livramento, as the right full-back, primarily oriented himself around Anderson and the right winger Elliott. In relation to Elliott, Livramento always behaved in a complementary manner: when one occupied the wide position, the other took up the half-space. It was also common for Livramento to invert and drop into the deeper half-space, with Elliott moving wider in response, and vice versa.

Anderson served as a secondary reference point. Whenever Anderson dropped back to form a wide back three, Livramento either moved inverted or stayed wide and deep. If Anderson remained central, Livramento positioned himself near the center-backs in the half-space, from where he could rotate forward into depth if the outside lane was free.

According to recent reports, on the left side, full-back Hinshelwood and winger Hutchinson rotated according to the same principles as Livramento and Elliott. Hinshelwood also frequently inverted into the deeper half-space or moved wide and deep. Both full-backs, Livramento and Hinshelwood, often initiated rotations through their inverted runs when the ball was with the near-side build-up player.

Runs into depth, however, were usually triggered only when other players moved to offer passing options. The No. 10 McAtee also played an important role as a reference point. When McAtee (and/or Hutchinson) moved into the left half-space, Hinshelwood rotated oppositely into depth.

McAtee, as a left-sided No. 10, had a freer role. He oriented himself around the holding midfielders to occupy or overload the central area when needed. He also rotated positions with left winger Hutchinson. Often, McAtee initially moved far into the left half-space to pull defenders out of the No. 10 zone behind him and then sometimes rotated further back toward the central center-back position.

It has been revealed that in response, either full-back Hinshelwood or holding midfielder Anderson rotated forward into depth. Alternatively, winger Hutchinson could rotate into the half-space, prompting full-back Hinshelwood to rotate wider.

Recent findings suggest that the English rotations created difficult conditions for Germany’s man-oriented attacking pressing. Man-marking was repeatedly manipulated, which in turn stretched and opened up spaces. Thanks to the flexibility of long balls and superiority in second balls, England’s build-up play additionally benefited in the first half. This led to repeated situations resembling counter-attacks, as England had plenty of central space available after bypassing the press.

In a recent development, the early goal also forced Germany to press higher more frequently and reduced their tendency to drop deep. Germany’s pressing behavior against England’s build-up thus became one of the decisive factors influencing the course of the game in the first half.

Author: MH is a football aficionado at heart. His apartment resembles a football library, with shelves filled with books on the great tacticians from Rinus Michels to Pep Guardiola. Of course, the book from Spielverlagerung.de is not missing. For MH, football is not just a game, it’s a way of life. He can be found on X under Mh_sv5 and LinkedIn.

#130576. What all 32 NFL teams should be thankful for this Thanksgiving

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2639 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

What all 32 NFL teams should be thankful for this Thanksgiving

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2639 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On an electric NFL Thanksgiving, I brought together my fellow CBS Sports writers Bryan DeArdo, Jordan Dajani, Carter Bahns and Garrett Podell to find one thing each team can be thankful for this holiday season.
  • The gap between the best team and the worst team in the NFL is quite large, but even though not all teams have the playoffs in their future, or even a winning record, they can still be thankful for what they do have,.
  • In a recent development, thanksgiving offers a natural opportunity to take stock of the good things, even during an NFL season that has not gone according to blueprint for every team.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On an electric NFL Thanksgiving, I brought together my fellow CBS Sports writers Bryan DeArdo, Jordan Dajani, Carter Bahns and Garrett Podell to find one thing each team can be thankful for this holiday season.

The gap between the best team and the worst team in the NFL is quite large, but even though not all teams have the playoffs in their future, or even a winning record, they can still be thankful for what they do have,.

In a recent development, thanksgiving offers a natural opportunity to take stock of the good things, even during an NFL season that has not gone according to blueprint for every team. Some franchises enter the holiday firmly in the Super Bowl race, while others are already measuring progress through young players, improved units and the draft capital that could shape a brighter future.

It has been revealed that winning despite turnovers – The Bills have a lot of reasons for gratitude. This one is somewhat of a good news, bad news situation: the team is turning the ball over more than they should, but they are still getting wins. It just goes to show that great teams will find ways to win games regardless. Josh Allen, James Cook, and their record are the obvious things they should be thankful for, but this one is most interesting to me because, as a team that has turned the ball over twice in three of the last four games and five times in a single game this season, 9-1 is impressive.

Industry observers note that drake Maye value – The Patriots have had a difficult season in terms of injuries, so much so that they're running out of spots on IR, and on-field struggles even when healthy. Quarterback Drake Maye is out for an extended period of time, likely the rest of the season, and without him the offense fell flat. The team still had their fair share of struggles with Maye, don't get me wrong, but if him being sidelined proved anything, it's how valuable he is to the team. In a season where many were questioning his real impact, wondering if last year was a fluke, the team can be grateful that when they do get Maye back (even if it's next year), the offense will be bumped back up.

Sources indicate that pass defense – The Jets are another team far outside the playoff race, but it's not all bad! Heading into Week 11, the Jets pass defense was fifth-best in the league, allowing 196.8 yards per game through 10 weeks. This alone won't get them to a Super Bowl, but on a team with many issues to point to, they can be thankful that something is working.

Forcing turnovers – Looking at the Dolphins record, it can be hard to think that they have anything to be thankful for. A high draft pick is one thing they can be grateful for, but so is their defense. They were tied for fifth-most interceptions with nine through 10 weeks and added two more against the Bills last week. The run defense had the challenge of facing Jonathan Taylor, Jahmyr Gibbs and James Cook and held them to under 100 yards each.

Joe Burrow — Cincinnati boasts a reinvigorated defense (led by Dexter Lawrence) and the best receiving duo in the NFL in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Burrow, however, remains the key to the Bengals' success. He's currently on pace to become the first player in history to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season while also completing at least 70% of his passes. He's among the MVP front-runners.

Todd Monken — With respect to John Harbaugh, Monken should win NFL Coach of the Year if the Browns continue to win. Cleveland is 6-4 and would be in the playoffs if the postseason started today. Monken has revived Deshaun Watson's career.

It has been revealed that jaylen Warren — Warren was arguably the biggest reason for Pittsburgh's 6-2 start. The former undrafted rookie rushed for over 700 yards over that span that included four 100-yard games. Warren and the Steelers' offense have fallen off in recent weeks, though. Warren becomes even more valuable within the offense as the Aaron Rodgers drama sparked a quarterback change.

Derrick Henry — While it's been a lost season in Baltimore, Ravens fans still get a chance to watch an all-time great do his thing. Henry is still playing well and setting new milestones in his 11th NFL season. This season, he's moved into third all-time in rushing touchdowns and seventh in career rushing yards.

Liam Coen – The Jaguars are now 20-7 under coach Liam Coen, who has turned this franchise from an afterthought to a Super Bowl contender. Coen has Trevor Lawrence finally living up to the lofty expectations set before him as a prospect coming out of Clemson, and has put together an impressive staff that includes defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile and offensive coordinator Grant Udinski. Both could be head coaches next year.

Sources indicate that C.J. Stroud – Imagine how disappointing the Texans would be this year if it weren't for the play of C.J. Stroud? He's thrown three touchdowns in three straight games, and scored at least two touchdowns in seven straight games. That's the longest such streak in franchise history. Stroud has thrown 22 touchdowns compared to just four interceptions this season. We no longer have to wonder if the Texans have a franchise quarterback.

The season is almost over – There are just six games remaining in the regular season. That's good news for Colts fans.

Future drafts – The one-win Titans traded away star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and safety Amani Hooker for some nice draft capital. Tennessee now holds four first-round picks and three second-round picks in the next two drafts, which could expedite a seemingly never-ending rebuild. As long as Mike Borgonzi doesn't draft another developmental pass rusher.

Patrick Mahomes back on top – The Chiefs are back and so is Patrick Mahomes. Kansas City's woes of last season are over, and the fans can breathe a sigh of relief that last year was a fluke. Mahomes has 22 touchdowns with just four interceptions this year, along with 2,709 yards. He is looking like the Super Bowl contender he has been in the past, and his offense has fixed many of the mistakes they had last season. With Mahomes playing like he is, this team has a real chance of going all the way.

Division still in reach – Last season the Broncos won the division, but that was with the Chiefs struggling. This year, K.C. is among the top in the league and Denver is still within reach of the divisional title. That is a major accomplishment for Sean Payton's squad.

Mendoza Era begins – The Raiders season has been filled with ups and downs. It started off strong, but then took a turn. The hope the Raiders and their fans can have is that the Fernando Mendoza era has begun and they can start to get excited about who they anticipate to be their franchise guy.

It has been revealed that high draft pick – The Chargers season hasn't been what they hoped, leaving lots of questions about their quarterback and coach. The good news is that they will be getting a high draft pick this year. Now they just need to do something with it.

John Harbaugh -- The Latest York Giants are fresh off a 23-18 win over the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) in Week 11 that has the Giants out to a two-game lead in the NFC East over the Cowboys.

It has been revealed that new coach John Harbaugh is pushing all the right buttons and has the Giants tracking toward a division title despite Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns suffering season-ending injuries within the first three weeks of the 2026 season. He is certainly someone the Giants are grateful to have leading their football team.

Dak Prescott -- Prescott is dragging his 29th-ranked scoring defense (28.4 points per game allowed) into the NFC East division race by powering the league's No. 4 scoring offense (30.6 points per game). Prescott became the fourth player in NFL history with 300-plus passing yards and five-plus total touchdowns in consecutive games across Weeks 10 and 11, per CBS Sports Research. He joined Daunte Culpepper (2004), Tom Brady (2007) and Ben Roethlisberger (2014) in this exclusive club.

Sources indicate that prescott now ranks second in the NFL in passing yards (3,049) and second in passing touchdowns (25) while ranking eighth in passer rating (101.0) and fourth in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.21). He is pulling off one of the NFL's biggest carry jobs this season, and he is someone that owner/general manager Jerry Jones should be eternally grateful to have leading his football team.

It has been revealed that jayden Daniels -- Daniels looks like his 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year self with all of his tools available to him. Daniels finished with 289 passing yards on 23 of 35 attempts while leading the Commanders with 55 yards rushing in a 22-20, buzzer-beating victory over the AFC North-leading Cincinnati Bengals. Washington now has consecutive wins over two first-place teams, the Giants and Bengals, no less, for the first time since the 2024 season, when Daniels won Offensive Rookie of the Year honors and the Commanders reached the NFC Championship Game.

After tossing a 32-yard game-winning touchdown to Stefon Diggs to shock the Giants and then the game-winning drive on Monday against the AFC North-leading Bengals, it's clear Daniels has his magic back.

Sources indicate that saquon Barkley -- The 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back powered the Philadelphia Eagles (75 rushing yards, including a 38-yard rushing touchdown, on 17 carries) to a 19-16 upset victory of the Pittsburgh Steelers to end the franchise's seven-game winning streak. Barkley is currently on a streak of four consecutive games with a rushing touchdown, the longest streak of his career in a lost year for his franchise.

It has been revealed that jahmyr Gibbs -- Gibbs leads the entire NFL in rushing yards (1,098), scrimmage yards (1,502) and touchdowns from scrimmage (15) through the first 11 weeks of the 2026 season. Gibbs is now the first player with 1,500-plus scrimmage yards and 15-plus scrimmage touchdowns through the first 10 games of a season since Emmitt Smith accomplished the feat in 1995.

Jeffery Simmons -- The Chicago Bears needed a game-changing presence along their defensive line, and All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons has been just that in his first three games. He racked up 3.0 sacks in Chicago's 21-13 Week 11 win over the Latest Orleans Saints, so Simmons is now up to 5.0 sacks and three consecutive wins in his three-game Bears career. Despite playing just three games with the Bears since coming over in a trade with the Tennessee Titans, he now co-leads his new team in sacks (5.0) with Austin Booker, who has played in all 10 games for Chicago this season. Simmons is now the only player in NFL history with five-plus sacks and three wins in his first three games after switching teams during a season,  according to CBS Sports Research.

Industry observers note that kirk Cousins -- Yes, the Minnesota Vikings are fresh off being steamrolled 35-10 on "Sunday Night Football" against the top-seeded San Francisco 49ers (9-1), but Kirk Cousins stabilizes their offense in a way Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz could not. He helped lead them to a 30-10 victory at the Green Bay Packers in Week 10 by doing just enough. Minnesota is in the NFC North division title race going forward because Cousins is a Viking once again.

Jordan Love -- Yes, the Green Bay Packers' patchwork offensive line didn't give Jordan Love (220 yards passing, one touchdown, one interception on 17-of-27 passing) a chance against Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense in Week 10 in a 30-10 defeat at Lambeau Field. He was sacked eight times, tied for the most in a single game this season with Deshaun Watson (twice) and Justin Herbert. Love made some strong throws when he had the time.

Industry observers note that A weak division – There has been no greater beneficiary of the NFC South's ineptitude since the start of 2025 than the Panthers. They won the division with a losing record last season and -- with their first-place standing at just 5-5 -- are on track to do so again in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that defensive improvement – For all the love the Vikings and Seahawks receive for their vicious defenses, it is actually the Buccaneers who lead the NFL in EPA per play allowed. Tampa Bay's unit has only gotten better as the season progresses and is on a new level right now, having forced at least four turnovers in each of the last three games. It also completed the only shutout of the season in Week 8.

Three optimism-inspiring wins – The losses have been bad. There is no way around that. But conversely, each of Atlanta's three wins is as stellar as the losses are concerning. The Falcons handed the Packers their worst loss of the year. They demolished the Saints for their only divisional victory. And they are responsible for the only blemish on the 49ers' resume. The lows might be low, but the highs prove that Atlanta can hang with anyone.

Jordyn Tyson's arrival from injured reserve – After he spent the first eight weeks of his career on IR, the No. 8 overall pick displayed all kinds of promise in two healthy games. He racked up 11 catches on 13 targets in his second outing, which is a massive workload for a rookie with only eight quarters of experience and one that suggests he could carry this offense if he stays in the lineup over the next month and a half.

Brock Purdy's career year – It will be difficult to outpace Joe Burrow in the MVP race, but Purdy is in the conversation. He was the catalyst behind the 49ers' stupendous first half of the season and is now the NFL's all-time leader in career passer rating, success rate and adjusted yards per attempt. Not bad for a former Mr. Irrelevant. Most impressive is that he is playing his best football while dealing with a plethora of injuries at wide receiver.

Quarterback depth – That Mike Macdonald had to assert that Sam Darnold is the team's starter when healthy is a testament more to Drew Lock playing up than Darnold playing down. Lock is 3-0 as a starter and won the season opener after taking over in the first quarter. To have someone capable of not only keeping the offense afloat when the starter is hurt but to thrive with a 125.6 passer rating is a major reason why Seattle is still in the postseason hunt.

According to recent reports, strength of schedule regression – If not for the highly manageable slate the Rams faced from Weeks 7-10, the conversation around Los Angeles would reek even more of disappointment than it already does. The combined records of the last four teams they played: 11-26-1. That was strong medicine for a preseason Super Bowl favorite that stunningly opened the year at 2-4.

Trey McBride – At least the Cardinals have a building block to construct a foundation around as they embark on their rebuild. Since Jeremiyah Love's rookie year has been a complete injury-riddled disappointment and the wide receiver group is torn down to the studs, it is a good thing McBride is around to provide some semblance of life on a team whose season is headed down the drain.

#130575. Meet Arjan Wijngaard, the man with 3,000 classic football kits in his possession

📅 25 Jan 2022 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1330 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thesefootballtimes ↗ Open Full Page

Meet Arjan Wijngaard, the man with 3,000 classic football kits in his possession

📅 25 Jan 2022 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1330 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thesefootballtimes

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • What do you do when you have nearly 3,000 football shirts in your possession?
  • Recently, These Football Times spoke to Dutch football shirt collector Arjan Wijngaard, the man behind www.voetbalshirts.org and the owner of one of the largest retro football shirt collections not just in the Netherlands but the whole of Europe.
  • It has been revealed that for nearly 25 years, Arjan has been collecting football shirts from around the globe, beginning with an Everton shirt that was given to him as a gift in 1997.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What do you do when you have nearly 3,000 football shirts in your possession? If your name is Arjan Wijngaard, the answer is allocate a room in your house as an exhibition space and log every single shirt in a comprehensive online catalogue.

Recently, These Football Times spoke to Dutch football shirt collector Arjan Wijngaard, the man behind www.voetbalshirts.org and the owner of one of the largest retro football shirt collections not just in the Netherlands but the whole of Europe.

It has been revealed that for nearly 25 years, Arjan has been collecting football shirts from around the globe, beginning with an Everton shirt that was given to him as a gift in 1997. With such an enduring reputation, we asked him what drew him to collecting kits in the first place.

According to recent reports, “The first question is the most difficult,” he says. “Of course, I liked football in the first place. That is an important thing if you want to collect football shirts. There is no particular reason why I chose shirts, though. Some people choose scarves (I have some scarves as well because if I can’t get a shirt when I visit a stadium or a game, I try to buy a scarf instead). Actually, maybe I’d better have chosen for scarves or pins; they are a lot cheaper and don’t need that much space!”.

According to recent reports, take a wander into Arjan’s shirt showroom and it is easy to see what he means. From ceiling to floor, the walls are fitted racks that groan beneath the enormous weight of his collection. The door is an incongruous rectangle of white in an otherwise ubiquitous banquet of colour, while in the window two mannequins stand sentinel in green and blue raiment. It is a veritable sacrarium to shirts – from clubs both grand and meek.

Industry observers note that “In general I like to collect shirts from clubs that are not very easy to find,” Arjan explains. “Like lower and non-league, for example, steps 9 and 10 of the [English football] pyramid or clubs from countries that are not known as famous football countries like Upcoming Zealand or Tanzania.”.

Not that anyone can turn up and take a tour around his showroom, however. Arjan makes extensive use of the internet to display his collection, for he runs a website – wherein he catalogues the shirts by country, club and division – as well as Twitter, Facebook and Instagram accounts all under the banner of Voetbalshirts.org. But what inspired him to begin this online odyssey in the first place?

Industry observers note that “There were a few reasons. Firstly, it is to show others what I have. Secondly, for the insurance to prove I had all the shirts if there is a fire or robbery. Also, having my collection online makes it easier for me to see what I’ve already got, especially when I am looking for newly introduced ones online and when I am in (fan) shops abroad.”.

These are the two main avenues through which Arjan acquires the vast majority of his shirts. Prior to the ongoing global pandemic, he was undertaking around five trips a year to foreign countries in order to expand his collection, with two or three of these visits occurring across the North Sea in Britain. But with flight restrictions hampering his ability to obtain shirts from the clubs themselves, he has made increasing use of the internet.

“I prefer to get them personally from the club shop near the stadium, but that’s not always possible with over 2,700 shirts,” he admits. “Other options are online club shops and, of course, eBay but also groups on Facebook and other collectors here in the Netherlands, abroad and on Twitter. During the years, I have made some contacts all over the world and that is also a fun part of collecting.”.

Indeed, Arjan is embedded deep in the football shirt community where he enjoys a prominent and active role as one of Europe’s most dedicated collectors. He presides over a football fiefdom of 6,000 followers across his three social media channels, while his website has attracted in excess of 200,000 visitors. But, he attests, the shirts themselves are not actually the most rewarding facet of being a collector.

Recent findings suggest that “All the things that come with collecting are maybe even nicer than having the shirts. The visits to the stadiums, searching online, getting in contact with people, meeting other collectors and also volunteers that are proud of their club and want to help me to add a shirt or their club to the collection is great. Shirt collecting got me a lot of positive things besides the shirts themselves. Lots of talking about shirts and football and helping each other through our mutual passion of football shirts.”.

In a recent development, as much as the community benefits are enjoyable, Arjan must have a favourite shirt, so we press him for an answer, hard as it may be to choose just one from 2,800 options. “There is one old FC Groningen shirt that is a favourite,” he admits at last, “because it is a rare one, matchworn and almost 40 years old.”.

Such a rare and antique shirt is the pride of his collection and, like most of his garments, Arjan refuses to wear it for recreational purposes, although not necessarily for the reason most people might expect. “I tend not to wear my shirts because not all of the shirts are in my size (anymore)!” he says. “I don’t wear football shirts very often. I don’t want to damage them. But, actually, some I have double: one for the collection and one to wear.”.

It has been revealed that even with such an extensive and valuable collection, Arjan still has his sights on expanding it further, even though his showroom appears to have reached the point of saturation. Even the door bears host to a number of caps hung on pegs hammered into the wood. He has a shortlist of kits he is working through and he reveals to us the one shirt he covets above all others.

“There is one shirt I really want to add to my collection, a matchworn Groningen cup final shirt from 2015. Groningen is my local team and they only won one trophy. The Dutch cup. And as I remarked before, I like shirts from non-league clubs I don’t have yet. So, if there are people who are reading this and think they can help me with a shirt from their local non-league club, don’t hesitate to contact me!”.

Recent findings suggest that situated as he is in the Netherlands’ north-east, Arjan’s local team and the one he professes to support most keenly is Groningen, best known in recent years for being the boyhood club of Arjen Robben. It was a love affair that began around 30 years ago and which served as something of a gateway into his lifelong affinity for the sport and the kits associated with it.

It has been revealed that “Groningen is my local team. I have had a season ticket for almost thirty years and the stadium is only ten minutes away by bike. My opinion is that you always have to support your local team. But Everton was my first shirt. I guess I like to support people’s clubs. Everton, Groningen and Feyenoord really are people’s clubs.”.

Though the boom in shirt collecting has been a relatively recent phenomenon, and one which was no doubt exacerbated by a lockdown that allowed people to invest more time and money in starting or expanding their collections, Arjan has been active on Twitter since 2010. He is, for all intents and purposes, one of the old guard, but what does the future hold?

“I have no aims to stop!” he confesses. “As long as I like it and have the space to continue, I shan’t stop.”.

MLB rumors: Blue Jays narrow focus, Cardinals target pitching, plus more relievers off the board

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The pre-Thanksgiving, pre-lockout free agent frenzy arrived this week.
  • Everyone is trying to squeeze in last minute signings and trades, and there could be a few deals on Thanksgiving.
  • Sources indicate that after landing Kaima Taira for five years and $80 million, the Blue Jays are expected to focus on adding offense, according to The Athletic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The pre-Thanksgiving, pre-lockout free agent frenzy arrived this week. Four of our top five, five of our top 10, and 20 of our top 50 free agents have already signed. You can be sure many more will come off the board between now and the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. The pitching market in particular has really moved.

Everyone is trying to squeeze in last minute signings and trades, and there could be a few deals on Thanksgiving. The hot stove pauses for no holiday. Here now are the Turkey Day rumors and moves.

Sources indicate that after landing Kaima Taira for five years and $80 million, the Blue Jays are expected to focus on adding offense, according to The Athletic. Toronto is not closing the door on adding more arms -- they remain engaged in the pitching market and have been connected to top free agent reliever Adrian Morejon -- but, with Taira aboard, offense is the greater priority moving forward.

The Blue Jays ranked dead last in runs and home runs in 2026. Catcher (Alejandro Kirk), first base (Vladimir Guerrero Jr.), and third base (Kazuma Okamoto) are the only positions Toronto can reasonably bank on above-average offense, and that's only if Vlad Jr. rebounds from his awful season. The Blue Jays need at least a corner outfielder. A second baseman wouldn't hurt either.

The Cardinals have checked in on free agent starters Shota Imanaga and Casey Mize, reports the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. They've also touched base with Shane Bieber. All three are among our top 50 free agents. Imanaga in particular has been a popular free agent. He's been linked to several contenders and is plenty familiar with the NL Central given his time with the rival Cubs.

Sources indicate that kyle Leahy, Quinn Mathews, Michael McGreevy, and Andre Pallante are penciled into rotation spots next year. Matthew Liberatore is still around, as is Richard Fitts for depth. St. Louis could use a veteran starter to help cover innings as they wait for top prospects Liam Doyle, Jurrangelo Cijntje, and Tekoah Roby to arrive. Someone to fill the role Dustin May filled in 2026, basically.

In a recent development, two 2027 postseason hopefuls added bullpen help late Wednesday evening. The Nationals agreed to a one-year, $5 million contract with lefty A.J. Puk, reports ESPN. There's an additional $2.5 million in incentives. Puk has not appeared in an MLB game since April 2025 due to UCL surgery and a shoulder capsule strain. Clearly, Washington expects him to be healthy in 2027.

The Twins, meanwhile, signed righty Kevin Ginkel, Puk's former teammate with the Diamondbacks, to a two-year deal worth $18 million, according to MLB.com. Ginkel, 33 in March, had a 5.01 ERA with Arizona over the last two years, though his under-the-hood indicators are much more promising. He'll join Yoendrys Gómez and Jeff Hoffman in Minnesota's late-inning mix.

It has been revealed that conversion rate has statistically been proven to be one of the best indicators for predicting a team’s success (Souza et al., 2019). All the more astonishing, then, that the underlying influencing factors are still largely unknown to most, leaving chance conversion for many as something of a black box. This analysis aims to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of goalscoring situations.

Chance conversion is most often associated with mental aspects. Accordingly, after defeats it is sometimes used as an excuse, partly due to a lack of more convincing alternative explanations. After all, the coach is said to have little or no influence on the psychological state of his players. Instead, the players are expected to learn how to better handle the pressure of a goalscoring opportunity, and in doing so become more efficient in front of goal.
