In het slechtste geval zorgt de zwakke counterpress van Oranje ervoor dat het onvoldoende dominantie kan ontwikkelen om Marokko langdurig op eigen helft vast te zetten. Daardoor zal Nederland minder tijd en balbezit rond het Marokkaanse strafschopgebied hebben en simpelweg te weinig kansen creëren om op basis van volume tot doelpunten te komen. Conclusie Voor Nederland is Marokko misschien wel de meest ongunstige tegenstander die het op dit WK kan treffen. Wanneer Marokko het dominante balbezitspel van het WK 2026 weet te combineren met het compacte lage blok waarmee het op het WK van 2022 zoveel succes had, Saibari als spits opstelt en Bouaddi de voorkeur krijgt boven Amrabat, dan is Oranje vanuit tactisch oogpunt eerder de underdog dan de favoriet. In dat scenario lijkt uitschakeling waarschijnlijker dan plaatsing voor de volgende ronde. HH groeide op vlak bij de Nederlands-Duitse grens, maar liet zich voetbaltactisch vooral inspireren door Zuid-Europa. Naast zijn werkzaamheden als freelancer voor Duitse profclubs is hij sinds twee jaar actief als jeugdtrainer van de O17 van N.E.C. Nijmegen. Artikel von Next Generation Wir rebooten Spielverlagerung. Unter der "Next Generation" veröffentlichen unsere neuen Autoren, Analysten und Trainer ihren Output. Einige von ihnen haben bereits Erfahrungen gesammelt, andere machen ihre ersten Schritte beim Erstellen von Artikeln. Nicht alle Beiträge werden schon ausgereift sein, aber zur Weiterentwicklung ihrer Verfasser finden wir es sehr wichtig, dass auch sie öffentlich verfügbar sind, um den Austausch und die Diskussion zu ermöglichen, die die Autoren weiterbringen. Daher möchten wir dafür werben, die Texte der "Next Generation" als Entwicklungsprojekt zu verstehen und am Prozessgedanken zu messen. Einige Artikel sind bereits auf dem Level, auf der Startseite von Spielverlagerung erscheinen zu können. Eine Übersicht sämtlicher Artikel der "Next Generation" findet sich hier.

Industry observers note that hoewel Nederland met een hoge laatste lijn en veel spelers rond de bal in theorie uitstekende voorwaarden creëert voor een effectieve counterpress, blijft de uitvoering wisselvallig. Na balverlies ontbreekt het nog te vaak aan directe druk op de bal. Daardoor krijgt de tegenstander regelmatig de mogelijkheid om de eerste pass vooruit te spelen voordat Nederland de controle terug heeft. Een deel van dat probleem ontstaat al tijdens het eigen balbezit. Wanneer Nederland te snel door het centrum probeert te spelen zonder eerst voldoende tegenstanders te binden, ligt de ruimte na balverlies direct open. Tunesië wist daar meerdere keren gebruik van te maken door met een numeriek overtal uit de eerste druk weg te spelen. Ook de restverdediging oogde niet altijd even stabiel. Doordat De Jong regelmatig uitzakte naast of tussen de centrale verdedigers, ontstond er soms een 4-0-structuur vóór de laatste lijn. De ruimte vóór de verdediging bleef daardoor onbezet, waardoor Tunesië na balveroveringen relatief eenvoudig de eerste pass kon versturen. Aké probeerde dat meerdere keren individueel te corrigeren door agressief door te stappen vanuit de laatste lijn. Zijn proactieve manier van verdedigen leverde verschillende balveroveringen op, maar bracht ook risico’s met zich mee. In de twaalfde minuut ontstond juist door zo’n uitstapmoment ruimte aan de buitenkant, waardoor Tunesië gevaarlijk kon omschakelen. Vergeleken met Van de Ven verdedigt Aké duidelijk aanvallender. Hij stapt sneller uit, durft vaker initiatief te nemen en wint veel duels vooruit. Tegelijkertijd vraagt die speelstijl om een perfecte onderlinge afstemming binnen de restverdediging.

Na rust verloor de counterpress geleidelijk aan kwaliteit. De afstanden tussen de spelers werden groter, waardoor het collectieve karakter steeds meer verdween. In plaats van gezamenlijk druk te zetten, probeerden individuele spelers het balverlies op eigen kracht te herstellen. Daardoor werd de restorganisatie minder stabiel en kreeg Tunesië vaker de mogelijkheid om onder de eerste druk uit te spelen. Ook de communicatie bij het doordekken liet in die fase te wensen over. Meerdere spelers twijfelden zichtbaar of ze moesten uitstappen of juist moesten terugvallen. Uit precies zo’n situatie ontstond uiteindelijk de corner waaruit Tunesië de aansluitingstreffer wist te maken.

According to recent reports, van alle mogelijke tegenstanders lijkt Marokko voor Nederland tactisch misschien wel de lastigste. Wanneer de Marokkanen het dominante balbezitspel van dit WK weten te combineren met de compacte verdedigende organisatie die hen tijdens het WK van 2022 zo sterk maakte, krijgt Oranje een bijzonder lastige avond. Vooral de manier waarop Marokko numerieke overtallen creëert, voortdurend van positie wisselt en spelers tussen de linies vrij probeert te spelen, sluit aan bij de kwetsbaarheden die Nederland in de groepsfase meerdere keren heeft laten zien. Daar staat tegenover dat ook Marokko niet onkwetsbaar is. Wanneer Nederland erin slaagt de eerste pressinglijn te omspelen en optimaal gebruikmaakt van de ruimtes achter de hoog doorschuivende backs, liggen er zeker mogelijkheden in de omschakeling.

It has been revealed that toch zal Oranje vooral zonder bal een vrijwel perfecte wedstrijd moeten spelen om controle te houden over de dynamische veldbezetting van Marokko. Op basis van de tot nu toe getoonde prestaties lijkt Marokko daarom eerder een zeer gelijkwaardige tegenstander dan een ploeg waar Nederland als uitgesproken favoriet aan begint.

LL ontdekte zijn fascinatie voor de inhoudelijke en tactische kant van het voetbal dankzij de vernieuwende ideeën van Thomas Tuchel bij Mainz. In de regio rond de Narrenstad deed hij al ervaring op binnen zowel het amateurvoetbal als de jeugdopleidingen van profclubs.

Marokko speelt op dit WK vanuit een 1-4-2-3-1, met een duidelijk aanvallend gekozen benadering. In de opbouw ontstaat met Mazraoui als linksback een asymmetrische driemanslijn. Die lijn positioneert zich vrij dicht bij elkaar, terwijl Hakimi een soort vrije rol krijgt doordat hij hoger doorschuift of juist naar binnen komt. Met zijn lange loopacties in de diepte zorgt hij voor veel dreiging. Door de hoge positie van Hakimi kan Brahim Díaz lager aan de flank komen, of juist ver naar binnen bewegen om als verbindingsspeler tussen de linies te fungeren. De twee beweeglijke controleurs vormen een compacte dubbele zes en creëren zo een soort 1-4-2-opbouw. Ze bewegen goed getimed kort horizontaal richting de flank, maken elkaar daarbij vrij en proberen het drukzetten van de tegenstander uit te lokken om daar vervolgens met korte combinaties onderuit te spelen. Aan de linkerkant beweegt El Khannouss eveneens wat lager, zodat hij aanspeelbaar blijft voor de naar binnen gekomen Mazraoui. Hij kan ook naar binnen bewegen om zo direct mogelijk in de halfspace open te draaien richting het doel. Tegen Haïti speelde Saibari in de laatste groepswedstrijd als nominale tien. In de andere wedstrijden fungeerde hij vaker als spits vóór Ounahi, die aan beide kanten dominant als verbindingsspeler aanwezig was. Saibari, als krachtige en dynamische loper in de diepte én als uitzakkende spits, stelt iedere verdediging ter wereld voor problemen. Tegen man-georiënteerde pressing, zoals Haïti bijvoorbeeld in de hoge pressing met een simpele man-tegen-man-aanpak deed, vormt de Marokkaanse structuur zich vaak richting een 1-4-2-2-2. Daarbij wordt de breedte op de hoogste lijn bezet, terwijl de tienruimte wordt overbelast en de centrale verdedigers van de tegenstander theoretisch zonder directe tegenstander op hun eigen lijn staan. Deze veelgebruikte structuur zal ook voor Nederland in zijn man-tegen-man-aanpak een uitdaging vormen. Ook buiten de lage opbouw gebruikt Marokko uitzakkende spitsen en dus korte passafstanden en overtal rond een flankspeler. Dat is eigenlijk simpelweg een voortzetting van de lokkende overtalopbouw. Tijdens de overgang naar voren, richting het laatste derde, schuiven de tienen en spitsen weer door naar de hoogste lijn. Verbeterpotentieel laat Marokko vooral zien in de manier waarop het in het overgangsspel deze doorschuivende bewegingen aan de laatste verdedigingslijn van de tegenstander beter kan verbinden en met passes kan benutten. Tegen Haïti lukte dat nog niet goed genoeg.

According to recent reports, als Nederland in het middenblok opnieuw prioriteit geeft aan het afdekken van de diepte achter de laatste lijn, dus niet met beide centrale verdedigers en backs doordekt, maar tegelijkertijd wel man-tegen-man druk wil zetten, zal Oranje waarschijnlijk voortdurend achteruit moeten verdedigen tegen Marokkaanse spelers die in de tussenruimte vrij kunnen opendraaien. Als de Marokkanen, die de flank zeer goed getimed vrijspelen en overbelasten — iets wat juist bijzonder ongunstig is voor Nederland, zoals in de vorige wedstrijden meerdere keren zichtbaar werd — er vervolgens in slagen om directer de doorschuivende bewegingen aan de laatste lijn van de tegenstander te vinden, kunnen ze Oranje tussen de linies volledig uit elkaar spelen.

In a recent development, nog gevaarlijker wordt het wanneer Marokko aan de flank of in de halfspace een ruit vormt. Binnen die structuur beweegt voortdurend een vijfde speler vrij. De speler aan de punt van de ruit zoekt met een loopactie de diepte om bijvoorbeeld de centrale verdediger en back te binden. Tegelijkertijd houdt de buitenspeler maximale breedte of komt hij juist in de bal om zijn directe tegenstander uit positie te trekken. De binnenste speler fungeert als verbindingsspeler, zodat het spel eenvoudig terug richting het centrum kan worden verlegd. De vijfde speler beweegt vervolgens precies in de ruimte die daardoor vrijkomt. Op die manier weet Marokko zich regelmatig vrij te spelen aan de flank. Van daaruit kunnen de spelers open draaien en optimaal gebruikmaken van de diagonale passlijnen die ontstaan. Dat maakt deze veldbezetting extra gevaarlijk, omdat de ploeg beschikt over meerdere creatieve dribbelaars die ook individueel een tegenstander kunnen uitspelen. Een nog groter probleem voor Oranje is dat Marokko aan beide kanten met een naar binnen gedraaide voet opbouwt. Aan de linkerkant gebeurt dat via El Khannouss en Mazraoui, aan de rechterkant via Brahim Díaz.

Slaagt Nederland er met de eerste pressinglijn – en dan vooral met Gakpo en Malen – niet in om op tijd een 2-tegen-1 te creëren tegen Díaz en El Khannouss, dan dreigt het numerieke ondertal in het centrum de verdediging te dwingen tot slecht getimede uitstapmomenten vanuit de laatste lijn. Gebeurt dat niet, dan bestaat het risico dat Marokko simpelweg door het centrum combineert. Kiest Oranje juist voor meer ondersteuning aan de buitenkant om daar de 2-tegen-1-situaties op te lossen, dan zullen de Marokkanen dankzij hun korte passafstanden, het constante overtal in de opbouw en hun bijzonder loopsterke dubbele zes nauwelijks onder druk komen te staan. Ook het Nederlandse principe om het spel bewust van buiten naar binnen te sturen, lijkt tegen deze tegenstander eerder een nadeel dan een voordeel. De centrale kwaliteiten van Marokko, gecombineerd met de positie van Mazraoui en zijn sterke rechtervoet, sluiten daar juist uitstekend op aan. Het voortdurend uitlokken van uitstappende verdedigers, de vele overtal­situaties, de creatieve dribbelaars, de goed uitgevoerde patronen richting de flank, de constante positiewisselingen en het gebruik van spelers met een naar binnen gedraaide voet maken Marokko tot een bijzonder lastige tegenstander voor de Nederlandse defensieve organisatie. Op dat vlak zal Oranje zich waarschijnlijk moeten aanpassen.

Industry observers note that verdedigend speelt Marokko meestal vanuit een ruimtegeoriënteerd 1-4-4-2, waarbij de nummer tien naast de spits komt te spelen. Tegen Brazilië probeerden de Marokkanen de Braziliaanse opbouw bewust naar hun linkerflank te sturen. Saibari positioneerde zich daarvoor aan de rechterkant hoger tegen de linker centrale verdediger van Brazilië. Mogelijk kiezen ze tegen Nederland voor dezelfde aanpak, om Van Dijk minder opbouwopties te geven. Binnen het 1-4-4-2 verdedigt de middenlinie vooral ruimtegeoriënteerd en veel minder vanuit mandekking. Regelmatig speelt Marokko daarbij op de grens van verticale oncompactheid, met name wanneer één of beide controleurs in het drukmoment moeten doordekken. De buitenspelers, Díaz en El Khannouss, kiezen juist voor bredere uitgangsposities om direct druk te kunnen zetten aan de flank.

Recent findings suggest that marokko onderscheidt zich de afgelopen jaren vooral door zijn defensieve intensiteit. Counterpress, sprints naar de bal, agressief doorstappen en het ondersteunen van ploeggenoten gebeuren allemaal op een hoog niveau. In combinatie met de bredere positie van de buitenspelers ontstaan daardoor kleine pressingvallen tussen de buitenspeler en de dubbele zes. Of dat volledig bewust gebeurt of niet, maakt uiteindelijk weinig uit: tegen Marokko krijg je meestal nauwelijks tijd of ruimte aan de bal. Toch kent ook deze manier van verdedigen zwakke punten. Bij het afschermen van de controleursruimte verdedigt Marokko niet altijd compact. Mazraoui stuurt El Khannouss regelmatig naar de zijkant om te voorkomen dat hij te veel ruimte moet verdedigen. Bij tweede ballen ontstaan daardoor geregeld grote gaten. Daarnaast zet de voorste lijn relatief weinig directe druk op de bal. De nadruk ligt vooral op het afsluiten van passlijnen en het sturen van de opbouw. Voor Oranje liggen daar zeker mogelijkheden, mits het de juiste pressingtriggers van Marokko weet te herkennen en te bespelen. Het overspelen van de eerste pressinglijn zou voor Nederland geen groot probleem moeten zijn. Daarna zal Oranje vooral moeten proberen de relatief zwakke linkerflank én de centrale verdedigers van Marokko aan het twijfelen te brengen: stappen ze uit of blijven ze juist staan?

Wanneer Marokko hoger druk zet, kunnen lange ballen bovendien een effectief wapen zijn. Ook Haïti kwam op die manier tot doelpunten. De laatste lijn van Marokko laat zich namelijk al vroeg terugzakken, terwijl de balnabije backs en de middenlinie – door het beperkte drukniveau op de bal – ver moeten uitstappen om hun directe tegenstander onder druk te krijgen. Daar staat tegenover dat Marokko tegen Haïti ook een goede tactische aanpassing liet zien met een sturend 1-3-1-4-2. De grootste kwetsbaarheid van Marokko ligt echter in het gedrag van de balverre spelers na balverlies. Zij leveren zowel in de counterpress als in het terugverdedigen nauwelijks ondersteuning. Dat valt vooral op aan de rechterkant wanneer Hakimi hoog op het veld staat.

Mocht Marokko er tijdens grote delen van de wedstrijd toch voor kiezen om terug te grijpen op de speelwijze uit het tijdperk van Regragui en te verdedigen vanuit een extreem compact en intensief 1-4-1-4-1- of 1-5-4-1-blok, dan wordt het voor Nederland bijzonder lastig om kwalitatief goede kansen te creëren. Breaking: Man for Man: How Brighton’s Press Suffocated Arsenal

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

von Next Generation am 23.09.2026 in den Kategorien Premier League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.

It has been revealed that brBrighton arrived at the match fresh off a 3–2 win at Old Trafford, while Arsenal boasted a clean defensive record and a reputation for controlling games and seeing them out like few other teams in Europe. The match ended 3–0, sparking immense hype around Brighton’s pressing. This analysis explores the underlying mechanisms: their man-oriented pressing across the entire pitch, their asymmetrical build-up play, their transition behavior after winning the ball, and the three goals themselves.

In a recent development, arteta’s Arsenal are among the best sides in Europe at controlling games out of possession. Any opponent who sets out to establish order is playing on the ground Arsenal own. Hürzeler therefore decided against control – not control surrendered in the sense of a low block, but a chaotic game state that Brighton generated themselves and were therefore prepared for.

System & movement with the ball – FC Arsenal.

System & movement with the ball – Brighton & Hove Albion.

The thread running through ninety minutes: Arsenal were not to settle into an organised phase either with or without the ball. Three decisions delivered that. The build-up was set up asymmetrically – on the right Brighton prepared the long ball and occupied the landing zone before it was played, on the left counter-movements opened the short route. It was never long instead of short, but two prepared options that would have demanded opposite answers from Arsenal. After regains the ball was not secured but risked immediately, because a secured ball gives the opponent exactly the seconds they need to reorganise. And the press lived off intensity and constantly new starting points: when a line was played through, Brighton did not stand still but re-established their shape and triggered again.

All three decisions give up ball control in the classical sense. Control came instead from preparation – if you know where the ball will land and you are standing there beforehand, you control the situation without the ball.

It has been revealed that what followed can be pinned to a single number: 41 Arsenal turnovers in their own danger zone. That is not a figure a side of this quality produces because they play badly, but because they never reached the game state their build-up is designed for.

Brightons manorientated press against a 4-3-3.

In a recent development, the press was simple in principle and demanding in execution. Brighton set up with man-reference to their direct opponent and switched into pure man-marking on the trigger. Against a side that tracks from the first second, marking assignments can be pulled apart by movement before any pressure exists; Brighton refused to offer that, because their shape stayed compact until the trigger moment.

In the “mid-block,” positioned +1 on the last line, but ready at any moment to transition into a high press upon a pressing trigger.

The steering began with Ayari. He curved his pressing run so that Konsa stayed in his cover shadow and Raya was forced to the other side. Kostoulas marked Gabriel, while Chema Andrés and Groß pushed aggressively onto Arsenal’s No. 8s. Groß in particular tracked the dropping Rice and at times advanced into the first pressing line, in some sequences all the way onto Konsa. That requires Rice to be picked up by a team-mate in the same moment – the man-marking worked through handovers as much as through tracking. Centrally, the striker and the No. 10 rotated accordingly: whoever had the shorter route to the next man on the ball pushed out, while the other covered behind him and took over again on the next trigger.

Recent findings suggest that it only held up because the centre-backs came with it. Vušković and Struijk stepped out onto Ødegaard and the dropping Havertz and prevented an underload in central areas. When Arsenal built with three in the first line, Brighton kept one centre-back zonal in the back line – but with permanent reference to the unmarked player in the No. 6 space, stepping onto him the moment the press was triggered. Arsenal’s numerical advantage in build-up therefore never translated into a free man anywhere on the pitch.

According to recent reports, raya was part of the marking scheme too. Ayari’s cover shadow left only the route through a No. 6, and under man-marking that is not an escape but a duel that begins with the first touch. Raya’s body shape reinforced it: he tended to open only half-way, which effectively removed the switch to the far side from his repertoire. Steered onto his right foot, only the right-hand build-up side remained; the left lay open for long stretches and was unreachable for the one player who could have found it.

Every back pass served as a trigger. When the ball went back to Raya or the centre-backs, Brighton pushed up as a unit and raised the defensive line. The density around the ball came less from the base shape than from the recovery runs: players who had been beaten sprinted back, and they did not run at the ball but with a cover shadow onto the lay-off option behind it. An Arsenal player with a marker in his back therefore had neither the lay-off nor the chance to turn.

It has been revealed that this is precisely where Brighton differed from most sides who get played through against Arsenal. The usual response is to stay deep once a line has been broken and wait for the shape to settle. Brighton instead pushed up into the next line and used the mid-block to prepare the next jump back into the high press – even when that press had just been beaten. The press therefore had not one starting point per possession, but a steady supply of new ones, and Arsenal had to solve the same pressure several times within a single attack.

Arsenal’s core problem was the absence of a threat in behind. Their attempts to play through the press came without pace beyond the back line, so Brighton were never forced to turn towards their own goal. That made the press cheap: no threat in behind, therefore no need to drop the line. There are three answers to committed man-marking – movement that drags your own marker away and opens space for a third player, a dribble that beats the assignment one-on-one, or a target man who wins the long balls. Arsenal produced none of them.

According to recent reports, when the high press was beaten, Brighton dropped into a 5-1-4 and inverted the priority. The five in the last line formed a deliberate overload against Arsenal’s front line – in exactly the moment a man-oriented side is most vulnerable, because its players are facing forward while the opponents are already moving. Brighton took the depth out of the situation first and only then thought about the ball again.

A “mid-block” in a 5-1-4 formation. The foremost players protected the “red zone” by using their cover shadows and shifting extremely compactly. Arsenal was mostly forced to play around the block, repeatedly giving Brighton time to reorganize.

A single No. 6 held the connection in front, while the four most advanced players stayed narrow and closed the centre with cover shadows rather than pressing the ball carrier. Arsenal found no central switch on the ball-near side and had to play around the block. Every trip around it cost seconds that Brighton used to shift across, so the end of the route offered the same congestion as the start. In some phases six players stood in the last line.

Industry observers note that the block was not a terminus. At every Arsenal back pass Brighton jumped out again and restarted the high press – the same trigger as in the high phase, only from a deeper starting position. The spare man in the last line made that possible, usually Vušković: because the overload left him without a fixed opponent, he could step out, cover the depth and pick up a man himself a moment later. That freed a midfielder to push forward without leaving an assignment open behind him – precisely the point at which sides with a similar approach usually come apart.

Recent findings suggest that in the “mid-block” phase, the “+1” players organized themselves to execute early handovers and jump into pressing situations. Here, Vuskovic—acting as the “+1” player from the defensive line—steps up to pick up the Arsenal player operating in the number 10 position.

According to recent reports, on top of that came the trap on the touchline. Once Brighton steered the ball wide, players jumped in from every direction: the ball-near winger closed the route back, the No. 6 covered inside, the back line stepped out. The back pass, the switch and the ball in behind did not disappear one after another but at the same time. Take away only the back pass and a side switches play; take away only the switch and they play backwards and start again. When all that remains is an individual action against several opponents with the touchline at your back, it almost always ends with the opposition.

It has been revealed that after a regain there are two basic options: risk the ball immediately to launch the attack, or secure it to establish order. Hürzeler consistently chose the first, and it follows directly from the overall idea – a secured ball would have given Arsenal exactly the seconds in which their structure reorganises.

When a high press was bypassed, Brighton succeeded in forcing Arsenal into congested situations in the area in front of the back four. In doing so, the players who had been bypassed shifted to block the passing lanes of the players positioned behind the ball. This created additional pressure on the ball carrier, who was simultaneously facing pressure from the front via a “negative” pressing movement (i.e., pressing towards their own goal).

Sources indicate that the counter was prepared before the regain. When Arsenal found a player in the No. 6 space after beating the press, Brighton immediately closed his back pass, so the turnover inevitably occurred in a moment when Arsenal were all ahead of the ball. The density around the ball, a defensive necessity, meant in attack that Brighton were central and therefore on the shortest route to goal. The first ball went to the deepest player, followed by a dribble at speed into the box, with no intermediate step and no square pass for safety.

Recent findings suggest that in the build-up phase, Brighton utilized a diamond shape. De Cuyper and Boscagli engaged in a 2v2 duel on the left flank, while Kostoulas, Gomez, and Kadioglu created a high 3v3 situation on the right. Briefly, both center-backs and a defensive midfielder would spread out to widen the formation. Additional support occasionally came from Groß, dropping back from the number 10 position. Ayari occupied Konsa and Gabriel through constant runs into the open spaces ahead of him.

Industry observers note that in deep build-up Brighton baited Arsenal in deliberately. Verbruggen put his foot on the ball while the centre-backs split and lengthened the pressing runs of their opponents. On paper that produced a 3v2 against Arsenal’s first line – except Hürzeler had no intention of playing through that overload on the ground. 25 of 40 goalkeeper passes were long, 62.5 per cent, and they went overwhelmingly to the right.

The structure allowed for a long ball to the right flank, feeding into the 3-3 formation. This created opportunities to contest the second ball or flick on the aerial pass. Additionally, Vuskovic offered a short, low passing option as the free player.

There, Brighton consistently created a 3v3 – an intact structure for the second ball regardless of whether the first contact was won. That is exactly what separates it from an ordinary long ball: the action was not judged by the aerial duel but by the situation that followed it. Kostoulas dropping added to the disorganisation of Arsenal’s high line, because a centre-back had to decide whether to follow him between the lines or let him turn. After winning second balls Brighton played on at high speed and looked for an early shot or an early cross, even against a defensive overload – again the decision for tempo over the clean attack.

Recent findings suggest that once again, the 3-3 structure on the right flank. Here, from open play.

On the left Brighton worked through pinning rather than through length. Boscagli stepping inside dragged Saka into central areas and took him out of the wide zone Arsenal needed him in defensively, while De Cuyper dropped and offered the mid-range diagonal once the assignments had been pulled apart. The asymmetry was a personnel decision: the players for second balls were on the right, the players who could drag markers out of position on the left. Arsenal would have had to condense against one side and hand over assignments cleanly against the other.

The team’s build-up play was asymmetrical, featuring a high, wide approach on the right contrasted with the left flank: Boscagli often played an inverted role—supplementing the existing diamond formation—which opened up space for de Cuyper. Meanwhile, Groß and Kostoulas occupied the players on Arsenal’s right defensive flank, enabling Brighton to find low-ball solutions against the press.

Recent findings suggest that with the ball in midfield there were two patterns. The first was the deliberate back pass to Verbruggen to pull Arsenal’s block out, followed by the same long-short structure as in deep build-up. The back pass was not a safety option here but the tool that created the space behind the pressing line in the first place.

It has been revealed that the second pattern worked through central and wide tension at high speed, supplemented by rotations within their own structure. Arsenal repeatedly failed to hand over their pressing assignments in a coordinated way against it – the same weakness Brighton had solved cleanly in their own press. In possession Brighton’s shape approached a 4-3-3: Chema Andrés as the deepest No. 6, Groß with freedom from the left half-space, Kadıoğlu pushing up early to support Gómez, Boscagli starting slightly deeper on the left.

In a recent development, the 1-0 by Groß in the 31st minute is the whole plan in one sequence. Brighton play back to the goalkeeper from midfield, go long, lose the first contact and win the second ball. After a phase of circulation the next attack meets a back line that has already been destabilised: Kostoulas drops, Arsenal’s midfield and Konsa step out, and Kostoulas lays the ball back against the direction of the pressure to Groß. Because Ayari runs in behind at the same time, Arsenal’s defenders drop – and Groß has the time for the shot from around 20 metres. In the build-up Brighton had used rotations to drag Guimarães over to the left.

Sources indicate that the opening goal stems from a positional attack. Kostoulas spots open space and makes a run into it. With a pass played across his standing leg, he feeds the ball to Groß in the space between the lines. As Groß takes a few quick touches and dribbles toward the defensive line, Gabriel and Calafiori drop back together, thereby opening up a shooting lane.

Industry observers note that the 2-0 by Kostoulas shortly before half-time follows the same logic from the opposite direction. After a set piece of their own, Brighton clear an Arsenal counter and transition again immediately, 4v5 in Arsenal’s half, and once more the shot comes from distance while the centre-backs drop off.

Much like the goal that made it 1–0, both defenders went to ground near the ball carrier, thereby opening up space for the goalscorer—this time arising from a transition situation.

Sources indicate that both goals share the same cause: Arsenal’s centre-backs stepped out too late to press the man between the lines. React only when the shooting motion starts and you cannot get into the block from 20 to 25 metres. What is striking is that this passivity is the same one Arsenal demonstrated in their own build-up – a side that does not leave its position to offer itself does not leave it to close down a shooter either.

The 3-0 by Chema Andrés came from a corner: Groß delivered from the left, Brighton had created an overload at the far post and protected it with two blocks, and Chema rose completely unmarked to head in off the inside of the post.

Recent findings suggest that two goals up, many sides would have defended deeper. Brighton came out with unchanged and at times higher pressing intensity, and the coordination was visibly drilled: marking assignments were swapped cleanly even in dynamic situations, and Arsenal’s structural adjustments were absorbed.

Arsenal had managed a few organised possession phases in Brighton’s half in the first period; in the second it became harder. In those phases they built with a back three, Rice as the third centre-back, Ødegaard dropping alongside Guimarães and the full-backs occupying the half-spaces. Arteta reacted around the hour: Zubimendi and Merino for Timber and Guimarães, with Rice moving to right-back, followed shortly by Gyökeres and Eze for Ødegaard and Tzolis. There was no noticeable effect, because the problem did not lie in the shape but in the assignments in front of it.

Sources indicate that there was also a layer that usually goes missing in analysis: Brighton used tactical fouls deliberately to stop Arsenal finding a rhythm. Arteta admitted afterwards that the game had been “very difficult to control”, pointing to lost first and second balls and to Brighton’s directness.

Sources indicate that arteta’s Arsenal being outplayed this clearly is rare. That it happened proactively and aggressively is rarer still – most sides who take something from Arsenal do it with a low block and efficiency. Hürzeler deliberately stepped back afterwards and praised his players’ courage, which gets to the heart of it: the strategy only works if eleven players are willing to carry it through in every single sequence.

In a recent development, the interesting question is where the idea came from. Chelsea were a common opponent: Brighton had 74 per cent possession there and lost 3-4 against a counter-attacking side – control right down to the numbers, without return. Alonso’s Chelsea tried the opposite route against Arsenal, a deliberate surrender of control, also without success. The likely derivation lies between the two: neither give up control nor chase it, but generate the unsettled game state yourself and be prepared for it.

It has been revealed that there is no reason for panic at Arsenal, but Arteta will need answers against a high press. The build-up was predictable for long stretches, and above all the direct option with pace in behind was missing as a threat. As long as that does not exist, a man-oriented press costs very little against this side.

For Brighton the open question is repeatability. Man-marking of this commitment, collective recovery runs with cover shadows and a touchline trap that requires everyone to trigger at once are hard to produce twice in an English week. Whether the blueprint works was answered on this afternoon. How often it can be produced will decide the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

It has been revealed that the massive moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”.

According to recent reports, glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”.

According to recent reports, while Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

Sources indicate that one of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi mentioned: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

Recent findings suggest that “If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi stated: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”.

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

It’s full time at GTech Stadium: Brentford 1 Sunderland 1.

City needed Donnarumma to spare their blushes with several good saves.

Brighton 1 Leeds 1. Pascal Gross missed a late sitter and Leeds are still winless in Brighton’s ‘new’ stadium in 11 visits.

It remains 0-0 so Spurs are goalless in three, both sides remain winless.

Industry observers note that iliman Ndiaye took a knock and has come off after treatment. He has sat on the bench, though, rather than headed down the tunnel, which suggests it is not an injury.

Enzo Le Fee equalises from the penalty spot.

VAR does not intervene after Lewis-Potter was penalised for holding. Le Fee chipped a pen straight at the keeper there last season.

Ellis Simms with the latest, clocking Donnarumma flush in the face with his close-range effort.

And it’s a third goal from a  left-back, but this time it’s the substitute Ben Chilwell.

Massive cheer for Phil Foden when he came on for Rayan Cherki. Cherki has been creative for City and this might be trying another mode of attack for Enzo Maresca or saving legs for the Champions League in midweek. They have two full days of rest before facing Porto on Tuesday.

The goal did go to Var for a possible handball by Williams, and it was ruled that the Wales international did handle it. Did look very harsh.

The major headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

Industry observers note that the English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

Industry observers note that “I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

Sources indicate that “I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”.

Sources indicate that maresca stated he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

In a recent development, palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

Depuis janvier 2026, Bilal Benkhedim (25 ans), l'ancien Vert, vainqueur de la Coupe Gambardella 2019, opère dans les rangs du Mouloudia Club d'Oran, club de la Ligue 1 algérienne. Après un début de saison en demi-teinte, il s'installe peu à peu dans son équipe. Après une première entrée en jeu le 30 octobre contre l'Olympique Akbou, il a été titularisé le 4 novembre contre MC Alger, et tout récemment, vendredi dernier, contre la JS Saoura. Lors de ce match remporté 3-1 par le Mouloudia Club d'Oran (désormais 3ème au classement), il a inscrit le 2ème but dans le temps additionnel de la 1ère mi-temps, d'un magnifique tir de l'angle de la surface dans un angle fermé.

Le but de Bilal Benkhedim, c'est ici.

La carrière de Bilal Benkhedim à l'ASSE :.

- 2016-2017 : U17 nationaux avec Jean-Philippe Primard : 20 matchs, 6 buts- 2017-2018 : U17 nationaux avec Razik Nedder : 18 matchs, 23 buts ; U19 nationaux avec Lilian Compan : 2 matchs, 1 but.- 2018-2019 : U19 nationaux avec Razik Nedder : 9 matchs, 7 buts, victoire en Coupe Gambardella ; N2 avec Laurent Batlles : 13 matchs, 3 buts.- 2019-2020 : N2 avec Razik Nedder : 11 matchs, 2 buts ; pro avec Claude Puel : 3 matchs en L1, 1 match en Europa League, 1 match en Coupe de la Ligue, 1 match en Coupe de France.- 2020-2021 : N3 avec Razik Nedder : 1 match, 1 but ; pro avec Claude Puel : L1 : 3 matchs- 2021-2022 : N3 avec Razik Nedder : 8 matchs, 1 but.

Au niveau professionnel Bilal Benkhedim compte donc 6 matchs en L1, 1 match en Europa League, 1 en Coupe de la Ligue et 1 en Coupe de France.

Dual passports matter continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND remarked the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

The Dutch football association KNVB introduced an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser said it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

In a recent development, “Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”.

Some players said they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius mentioned he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

It has been revealed that “I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that claims I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”.

Alors qu'il vit sa 4e saison (sur les 5 dernières) en Ligue 2, le supporter stéphanois a développé une théorie selon laquelle tous les adversaires jouent le match de leur vie à Geoffroy Guichard.

Ce soir le Nantes de Grégory Poirier (avec Cafaro mais sans Sow, blessé au genou) - autre club historique plongé dans l'enfer de cette division - a l’occasion de revenir à 16pts des Verts, en cas de victoire à domicile contre le Grenoble d’Yvann Maçon (et de Jules Mouton non convoqué).

Interrogé en conférence de presse sur les difficultés des Canaris à s’imposer à la Beaujoire (1 victoire en 6 matchs), le coach nantais a également fait sienne cette fameuse théorie :.

« On le voit souvent, beaucoup d’équipes font leur meilleur match à l’extérieur à Nantes ou à Saint-Etienne parce que c’est un rendez-vous qu’ils ont coché, et ça il faut l’accepter on doit jouer avec ça. ».

Heureusement à Sainté, les hommes de Cathro l’ont manifestement mieux accepté avec 6 victoires en 6 matchs à GG.

Sources indicate that la Lazio di Gattuso ha raccolto nelle prime dodici giornate più punti di quella del 2000, considerata tra le più forti della storia biancoceleste per l’organico al completo. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Da quando la vittoria vale tre punti, soltanto la Juventus, prima con Capello e poi con Allegri, ha fatto meglio. According to recent reports, il confronto con la squadra del secondo scudetto riguarda anche lo spogliatoio. Gattuso vi ha portato un clima che richiama, con le dovute proporzioni, quello creato da Eriksson ventisei anni fa. Nella Lazio di allora, però, l’armonia non era quella di oggi: convivevano il gruppo degli ex Samp, guidato da Roberto Mancini, e quello degli argentini, senza un capo designato ma rappresentato dalle personalità di Veron e Simeone.

Il paragone suggerito dalla partita contro il Lecce è quello tra Belahyane e Almeyda. Il marocchino intercetta palloni e li sottrae agli avversari commettendo raramente fallo, come faceva l’argentino. Almeyda era chiamato Capitan Uncino per il modo in cui usava il piede destro per portare via il pallone; Belahyane si affida invece alla rapidità della corsa e all’appoggio del corpo sul rivale per interrompere l’azione.

Sources indicate that tra i portieri, Mandas richiama Luca Marchegiani: entrambi efficaci tra i pali, dotati di personalità sulle palle alte e meno talentuosi nel gioco con i piedi. A Marchegiani costò il posto in Nazionale un errore che Sacchi non gli perdonò.

Il ceco era un attaccante aggiunto per Zoff ed Eriksson; Davide è l’incursore della squadra di Gattuso. Alcuni movimenti di Taylor richiamano Stankovic, più potente soprattutto nel tiro dalla distanza. Aspect analysis: Leipzig never found a trigger – LC

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1476 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • von Next Generation am 20.10.2026 in den Kategorien Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.
  • In a recent development, A 6-1 reads like a game in which everything fell apart.
  • This aspect analysis therefore takes the goals rather than the game as its material and works back from there to the patterns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

von Next Generation am 20.10.2026 in den Kategorien Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.

In a recent development, A 6-1 reads like a game in which everything fell apart. Look at how the goals came about one by one and a different picture emerges: it was not six separate problems but two or three, which Bayern punished in seven variations. No pressure on the man in possession, marking problems in central areas, and a back line that did not work with the movements in front of it – that chain runs through practically every goal conceded.

This aspect analysis therefore takes the goals rather than the game as its material and works back from there to the patterns.

Industry observers note that bayern triggered very high throughout, stayed tight to their opponents and pushed through centrally without hesitation. Vandevoordt was pressed from Bayern’s right, with the clear intention of keeping him away from the left-hand build-up route and forcing the long ball. Leipzig’s front line of Nusa and Brajan Gruda repeatedly angled their runs deep against Nathaniel Brown and Konrad Laimer.

It has been revealed that bayern had one extra central player dropping into midfield in this phase, usually Kimmich. Had Leipzig played short to the right, he could have pressed through onto Raum; in practice he stayed central and pushed through from there. That left Leipzig with the long ball, and it was ineffective: it produced almost no regains, so the enforced forward play brought neither relief nor territory.

According to recent reports, going the other way, Leipzig got no access at all, and the reason was Bayern’s rotations. Kimmich dropped right, Pavlović left into a back three, with Upamecano holding a very wide position. Against this shifting three-man build-up Leipzig never found a trigger, because the assignments reset with every rotation – whoever was supposed to step out of midfield first had to work out who he was picking up. The handover of pressing duties out of central areas failed repeatedly.

In front of that, Bayern staggered their shape so that Leipzig’s compactness became the problem. Olise moved into the ten space at times, Nathaniel Brown operated in the half-lane and ran beyond from there, Luis Díaz stayed wide left. Saibari and Kane pinned several opponents centrally while regularly pulling out of the central lane. Because Leipzig pressed very narrow, this produced exactly what Bayern were looking for: once the opponent was committed near the ball, the switch followed, and on the now open side stood a one-on-one.

It has been revealed that that already builds the bridge to the goals. The isolated one-on-ones in which Luis Díaz got his three finishes were not individual moments but the product of this sequence of pinning and switching.

1-0, Luis Díaz (12.) – The first goal already contains the full diagnosis. Kimmich receives centrally without any pressure and can turn out with an open body shape. Ahead of him Saibari and Kane occupy the central zone in front of the box, which forces Orban and Lukeba to step out – so far, the intended part. The full-backs, however, do not push up with that movement and stay too deep, while Raum’s position plays the runner onside. Klostermann stays outside and leaves the inside lane unsecured, and that is exactly where Luis Díaz starts from. Out of that unprotected lane Díaz runs into the back line and Kimmich chips the ball in behind. Not one bad decision, but four players whose decisions did not fit together.

Industry observers note that 2-0, Aleksandar Pavlović (26.) – Same cause, different route. Kane drops deep and Leipzig do not shift across as a unit – the reactions indicated it clearly: arms thrown up, gesturing, hands dropping again, the beginnings of frustration. Kane gets the free body shape, and with him the consequence is predictable: the long ball, high or flat. Because Leipzig are so narrow centrally, the ball flies straight through the entire zone in front of their back line. Luis Díaz moves actively into the passing lane to control it while Klostermann tries to get into his running line and does not make it – Díaz reaches the ball first. From the one-on-one he wins, Díaz dribbles centrally at Orban, which creates a four-against-three on the break. Díaz pins Orban and Lukeba centrally, Pavlović overlaps on the left after holding a high, left-leaning position all evening and threatening the back line. Two touches, left foot, finished away from the defender.

3-0, Michael Olise (34.) – Here Bayern’s press highlights itself at its clearest. From a Leipzig throw-in, the man-orientation is fully visible: consistent pushing through, clean handovers. A misplaced pass from Raum then cannot be defended, because neither the tracking nor the duelling is good enough to disturb the pass. Kane can open up half-way. Centrally, Olise comes inside from the wing, and Banzuzi and his partner fail to pick him up, letting him run through – against a player of that variability, an invitation to the key pass. Luis Díaz runs beyond and drags Orban with him, Klostermann is pinned wide by Saibari and can no longer get back into central areas. Olise finishes against the goalkeeper’s movement, across his standing leg into the far corner, catching Vandevoordt completely on the wrong foot.

In a recent development, 4-0, Luis Díaz (47.) – After a regain, Bayern switch promptly to the far side and once diagonally through, putting Díaz in a one-on-one again. He holds the ball in the dribble, and Leipzig fail to solve the situation in three steps: the centre is not closed, Orban is too late stepping out, Klostermann does not get into the duel. That Vandevoordt leaves the far corner open is the final piece of an isolated one-on-one that should never have arisen.

It has been revealed that 5-0, Harry Kane (53.) – Structurally the most interesting goal. Leipzig play a long ball without preparing it and react to the consequences contradictorily: the back line does not push up at all, while the midfield line and both forwards counterpress forwards. The ten space opens up enormously, the gaps between the lines become huge – and Olise is standing in that zone. One pass from Kim is enough to take six Leipzig players out of the game. Olise runs unopposed at the back line and lays it off to Díaz, who is in a one-on-one again; Brown joins for the two-against-one and shifts into the inside lane. Klostermann does not pick up his run from the deep half-space, and centrally Kane again drops into Orban’s blind side – a pattern that stood out across the whole game. The result is a two-against-one against the goalkeeper.

6-0, Luis Díaz (69.) – From a set piece Bayern create a five-against-four out wide. Gnabry pins opponents and makes the space for Díaz, Orban again takes one substantial step in the block and does not get into the duel. The same scene as the 4-0, only from a different phase of play – a sign that this is a behavioural pattern rather than a snapshot.

Sources indicate that 6-1, Andrija Maksimović (90.+1) – Leipzig’s goal highlights in reverse what their own game had been missing. Bayern drop into a deeper block here, and Leipzig combine centrally before going wide. Gruda gets into a one-on-one against Brown, Upamecano steps across – but from above, with too wide a gap and without closing the centre. That opens the one-two, which Leipzig take immediately. Because the whole situation narrows onto that combination, the space behind it stays unoccupied, and Maksimović can take two touches on his left and finish unopposed.

Recent findings suggest that the sequence of goals reads like a repetition. Five of Bayern’s six come from the same combination of no pressure on the ball centrally and a back line that does not manage the space behind it. Luis Díaz stands in an isolated one-on-one three times, Orban is twice too late with a step that is too major, Kane repeatedly drops into his blind side. Klostermann certainly did not have his best day – but it would be too easy to settle the bill with him. In the decisive scenes he faced situations that functioning protection in front of him should never have allowed to arise in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that behind it all lies not an individual problem but a structural one: Leipzig pressed narrow and found no trigger against Bayern’s rotating back three. That very compactness made the switch of play the opponent’s most effective tool, and at the end of every switch stood a one-on-one that Leipzig lost. The scoreline is not the story – the story is that the same scene worked six times.

Promu en Ligue 1 en mai dernier au nez et à la barbe d'un club formateur qui ne lui aura guère fait confiance (8 minutes temps additionnel compris en équipe première contre le QSG dans le Chaudron le 28 novembre 2021), Lucas Calodat (24 ans) a vu sa valeur multipliée par 30 depuis qu'il a quitté Sainté l'été 2023. Il est en effet estimé par Transfermarkt à 3 M€, soit 1,2 M€ de plus que le joueur qui occupe actuellement son poste chez les Verts (Ben Old, de la même génération 2002).

Meilleur joueur sarthois de la saison en cours et 34e meilleur joueur de l'élite selon Sofascore (ex aequo avec le capitaine du Paris FC Pierre Lees-Melou et celui des vilains Corentin Tolisso), le dynamique piston gauche manceau a brillé hier sous un maillot vert et blanc au Vélodrome où il s'est imposé en clôture de la 11e journée de L1 sous le regard aussi médusé que consterné de Théo Vermot et Neal Maupay (restés sur le banc phocéen) car l'OM menait encore 2-0 à la 70e minute...

Industry observers note that la Pravda lui donne la meilleure note de cette rencontre (7/10), assortie du commentaire suivant : "Oui, le travail défensif est parfois un peu aléatoire, il a oublié Amine Harit (7e) et n'est peut-être pas net au départ de l'action qui a amené le second but de l'OM. Mais quelle débauche d'énergie et quel pied gauche ! Capable d'éliminer Harit avec aisance (17e). Un centre bien travaillé vers la tête de Gueye, non cadrée (28e). Une bonne incursion et un bon ballon pour Gueye (45e+1). Un centre mal exploité (64e), mais c'est lui, du pied droit, qui a trouvé Colas pour l'égalisation (2-2, 84e).".

Ouest-France considère que le natif de Paris a été le meilleur à Marseille. Le quotidien régional le plus diffusé de France lui décerne en effet un joli 8/10. "Il a réussi un match plein, ce en quoi il pêchait jusque-là. Technique face à Harit, auteur de deux beaux centres pour Gueye (27’, 45’+ 1). Il relance surtout le match en offrant la passe décisive de l’égalisation.".
